messages.subject: quantile normalization target distribution
messages.body_plain:
Hi Henrik,

While processing a sample of ~150 cel files with aroma.affymetrix for
a CNV analysis,  I ran into a problem comparing normalized intensities
between groups of Affy 500K cel files that were collected over two
different time periods and from two different labs.   The problem
appears as a high correlation of the 500K normalized intensities
("theta") within groups (~0.6) but a low correlation between groups
(~0.0).

I was ready & willing to chalk this up as a lesson in the batch effect
and to redefine the raw copy number reference intensity in some way
that doesn't cross batch boundaries.  However,  a colleague suggested
that the problem might be remedied by redoing the quantile
normalization step with a target distribution built from  Hapmap
samples only.    Although I can't claim to see how this would remedy
the situation, I also don't see how to test the hypothesis using the
aroma.affymetrix package framework.    Is there a procedure for
extracting an average intensity distribution from a subset of arrays
and then using it in
QuantileNormalization(...,targetDistribution=...)?

Thanks much,

Chip Stewart

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] quantile normalization target distribution
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Sat, Mar 1, 2008 at 12:40 PM, Chip S <Donald.A...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>  Hi Henrik,
>
>  While processing a sample of ~150 cel files with aroma.affymetrix for
>  a CNV analysis,  I ran into a problem comparing normalized intensities
>  between groups of Affy 500K cel files that were collected over two
>  different time periods and from two different labs.   The problem
>  appears as a high correlation of the 500K normalized intensities
>  ("theta") within groups (~0.6) but a low correlation between groups
>  (~0.0).
>
>  I was ready & willing to chalk this up as a lesson in the batch effect
>  and to redefine the raw copy number reference intensity in some way
>  that doesn't cross batch boundaries.  However,  a colleague suggested
>  that the problem might be remedied by redoing the quantile
>  normalization step with a target distribution built from  Hapmap
>  samples only.    Although I can't claim to see how this would remedy
>  the situation, I also don't see how to test the hypothesis using the
>  aroma.affymetrix package framework.    Is there a procedure for
>  extracting an average intensity distribution from a subset of arrays
>  and then using it in
>  QuantileNormalization(...,targetDistribution=...)?

Yes, although yet not streamlined, it is possible.  The easiest way is
to pass a vector of intensities via 'targetDistribution'.  The default
of QuantileNormalization is to normalize all probes, but if you only
normalize based on say PMs, you have to make sure to pass only  PM
values in 'targetDistribution'.  The 'targetDistribution' represent a
distribution so its values will be sorted internally.

So, here is an example calculating the target distribution from the
HapMap samples and then uses it to normalize your test set:

csHapMap <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("HapMap270,500K",
chipType="Mapping250K_Nsp");
yTarget <- averageQuantile(csHapMap);

qn <- QuantileNormalization(cs, targetDistribution=yTarget, tags="*,HapMapRef");
rm(csHapMap, yTarget); # Not needed anymore

csN <- process(qn);

Hope this helps.

/Henrik

>
>  Thanks much,
>
>  Chip Stewart
>  >
>

messages.body_plain:
On Sat, Mar 1, 2008 at 10:10 PM, Yue Hu <yuehu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> region.xls file contains information like the following,  what is the
> meaning of mean and count?  How to calculate copy number of each region?
>
> sample    chromosome    start    stop    mean    count    url
>  NA07029_GW6_C    1    51599    557616    -0.175    35
> http://genome.ucsc.edu/........
> NA07029_GW6_C    1    593454    6573438    0.01    3171
> http://genome.ucsc.edu/........
>  NA07029_GW6_C    1    6573680    6574130    1.158    2
> http://genome.ucsc.edu/.........

The 'mean' values are the mean raw CN level for the region and 'count'
is the number of loci in the region.

You did not tell us what segmentation method you used, but neither the
GLAD nor the CBS method tries to *call* the "true" underlying copy
number in {0,1,2,...} copies but only returns a *mean estimate* on the
continues scale.  GLAD can call regions as loss, normal, or gain
though.  See the references for those two methods for explanations.

/Henrik

>
>
> Thanks!
>
> Yue
>

messages.subject: Bug fix: Latest UGP annotation file for GenomeWideSNP_5 was broken
messages.subject_clean: Bug fix: Latest UGP annotation file for GenomeWideSNP_5 was broken
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

the UGP annotation file GenomeWideSNP_5,Full,r2,na24,HB20080214.ugp is
broken because all loci on Chr10 are recorded as Chr13 loci.  This
error was not in UGP files preceeding this one. The mistake has been
corrected in GenomeWideSNP_5,Full,r2,na24,HB20080302.ugp.  Please
download the latter from the group page and discard the former.

If you've done CN analysis using the broken UGP file, this should only
affect the segmentation on Chr10 and Chr13.  In other words, it is
enough to redo the segmentation for these two chromosomes by using
arguments 'chromosomes=c(10,13)' and 'force=TRUE'.

/Henrik

PS. Technical details/for the record: My best guess is that byte
values 10 (0x0a) have been replaced by values 13 (0x0d) while
transferring the file between Windows and Unix as a text file and not
as a binary file. I've checked the UGP files for the other chip types
and they are correct. DS.

messages.body_plain:
Dear Henrik

Thank you for your detailed reply, getRegions() was the method I was
looking for.

The method writeRegions() is also very convenient, since it exports
the results as an Excel-file:
However, running your example:

> pathname <- writeRegions(glad, arrays=1, chromosomes=1:4, organism="Human", hgVersion="hg18")

and opening the Excel-file I realized that the Excel-file contains
already data for all arrays and all chromosomes,
and added the new results at the end. It seems that I did already have
this Excel-file and new data are always appended.
Is this corect?

Furthermore, I get the following result for one region:
	mean	count call
	-4.402	5	loss
I suppose, that 'mean' is the log2ratio of the mean raw CN levels,
e.g. log2(0.1/2)=-4.32, thus mean CN=0.

Although you mention that getRawCnData() is not a public method, I am
curious:
How do I get (a list of) ChipEffectFiles?

Finally, please allow me to make a comment, since getRegions() is a
good example of my problems:
Since most methods are not explained in the help file, I need to look
at the source code, e.g.file CopyNumberSegmentationModel.R:

- setMethodS3("getRegions", "CopyNumberSegmentationModel",
function(this, ..., url="ucsc", organism="Human", hgVersion="hg17",
margin=10, flat=FALSE, verbose=FALSE)
is not documented, and there is no hint that I can pass parameters
arrays and chromosomes to this method. Thus I could not see that this
method would be the one I need.

In contrast,
-  setMethodS3("fit", "CopyNumberSegmentationModel", function(this,
arrays=NULL, chromosomes=getChromosomes(this),
force=FALSE, ..., .retResults=FALSE, verbose=FALSE)
is documented and shows that I need parameters arrays and chromosomes.

Since there are hundreds of methods it would be helpful to know which
methods are public and which ones are private (i.e. for internal use
only). Furthermore, it would be helpful if the public methods would be
explained in help files.

Best regards
Christian

messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: How to extract copy-numbers from glad model
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Mon, Mar 3, 2008 at 3:50 AM, cstratowa
<Christian...@vie.boehringer-ingelheim.com> wrote:
>
>  Dear Henrik
>
>  Thank you for your detailed reply, getRegions() was the method I was
>  looking for.
>
>  The method writeRegions() is also very convenient, since it exports
>  the results as an Excel-file:

It is not really an Excel file but a tab-delimited file with file
extension *.xls for easy opening in Excel (inspired by how dChip does
it).

>  However, running your example:
>
> > pathname <- writeRegions(glad, arrays=1, chromosomes=1:4, organism="Human", hgVersion="hg18")
>  and opening the Excel-file I realized that the Excel-file contains
>  already data for all arrays and all chromosomes,
>  and added the new results at the end. It seems that I did already have
>  this Excel-file and new data are always appended.
>  Is this corect?

I guess that is the current behavior.  writeRegions() is also called
everything you do process() via the ChromosomeExplorer.  I guess that
is what you've done and the reason for why you already got results.
For safety, I guess I decided to append data rather than overwriting
it.

>
>  Furthermore, I get the following result for one region:
>         mean    count call
>         -4.402  5       loss
>  I suppose, that 'mean' is the log2ratio of the mean raw CN levels,
>  e.g. log2(0.1/2)=-4.32, thus mean CN=0.

First of all, note that the log-ratio scale has *not* been calibrated
to be linear with the true underlying copy number.  This is because we
do not have a way to do this calibration in a random data set.  The
only thing done is to rescale the CNs across arrays such that diploid
loci are likely to have log-ratio 0.

Second, as a wrote in a different thread on a related question,
*calling* copy numbers {0,1,2,...} is much harder and relies on more
assumptions such as homogenuous cells and so on.  This is the reason
why the CN is reported on the continuous scale.  GLAD tries to
classify regions as loss, normal, and gain, but it is done in an "ad
hoc" way so you should rely on those calls blindly.

>
>  Although you mention that getRawCnData() is not a public method, I am
>  curious:
>  How do I get (a list of) ChipEffectFiles?

If you get the ChipEffectSet, which you pass to the segmentation
model, then you get the files as list by calling getFiles().  [There
is also as.list() but I'm not sure if that is a good name to be kept.]

>
>  Finally, please allow me to make a comment, since getRegions() is a
>  good example of my problems:
>  Since most methods are not explained in the help file, I need to look
>  at the source code, e.g.file CopyNumberSegmentationModel.R:
>
>  - setMethodS3("getRegions", "CopyNumberSegmentationModel",
>  function(this, ..., url="ucsc", organism="Human", hgVersion="hg17",
>  margin=10, flat=FALSE, verbose=FALSE)
>  is not documented, and there is no hint that I can pass parameters
>  arrays and chromosomes to this method. Thus I could not see that this
>  method would be the one I need.
>
>  In contrast,
>  -  setMethodS3("fit", "CopyNumberSegmentationModel", function(this,
>  arrays=NULL, chromosomes=getChromosomes(this),
>  force=FALSE, ..., .retResults=FALSE, verbose=FALSE)
>  is documented and shows that I need parameters arrays and chromosomes.

For maintainance and quality reasons I try to keep code redundancy to
a minimal.  This will also minimize the risk for having the same bug
in multiple places.  One way to to minimize redundancy is to pass
arguments handled by other methods via '...'.  I do try to write in
the Rd help where '...' is passed to so one can follow the arguments a
bit easier.  Although, it is not unlikely that there are places where
code have changed but the docs lag behind.

>
>  Since there are hundreds of methods it would be helpful to know which
>  methods are public and which ones are private (i.e. for internal use
>  only). Furthermore, it would be helpful if the public methods would be
>  explained in help files.

Sure indeed.  However, last time I checked (April 2007) the source
code and the Rd files filled almost one thousand (=963) pages.  There
is basically no chance/time for me to keep everything up to date.

Someone ones said "who needs documentation when you've got code".  I
guess it applies here.  To be more serious, you probably should trust
the code to be more up to date than the Rd help.  What you can trust
in the Rd help is that the usage, the list of arguments are correct
and example code, because that is validated while building the
package.

So the strategy I use instead is that what is documented on the group
pages show the part of the API that you can expect to be rather stable
and be around for a while.

Via the R.oo framework I also "tag" methods as private, protected, and
public.  Example:

> methods("getRegions")
[1] getRegions.CopyNumberSegmentationModel
[2] getRegions.profileCGH
> attributes(getRegions.profileCGH)
$modifiers
[1] "private"
> attributes(getRegions.CopyNumberSegmentationModel)
$modifiers
[1] "public"

These tags are not really up to date all the time, because if not
specified explicitly in the code they default to "public".  However,
whenever you see a "private" or "protected" tag, you should be careful
using it in your code without asking first.  Consider them as internal
support functions of aroma.affymetrix that have their own life.  If
aroma.affymetrix ever get a namespace, the private methods are the
first ones to "disappear" (=not be exported).

Having said all this, contributions/corrections are welcome and appreciated.

Cheers

Henrik

>
>  Best regards
>  Christian

>

>  >

>  >
>  > >  > Using aroma.affymetrix I have fitted a GLAD model and would like to extract
>  > >  > the (relative) copy-numbers.
>  >
>  > >  > Following the aroma-affymetrix website I did:
>  > >  > # get cdf

>  > >  > > cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chiptypes[1])
>  >
>  > >  > # get cel
>  > >  > > name <- "TestSty250K"
>  > >  > > cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chiptypes[1])
>  >
>  > >  > # correct for allelic cross talk
>  > >  > > acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs)
>  > >  > > csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose)
>  >
>  > >  > # quantile normalization
>  > >  > > cs.ac <http://cs.ac> <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, tags="ACC,-XY",
>  > >  > > chipType=chiptypes[1]) ac.qn  <- QuantileNormalization(cs.ac <http://cs.ac>) csCN <-
>  > >  > > process(ac.qn, verbose=verbose)

>  >
>  > >  > Since ChromosomeExplorer can use the copy numbers for display, my question
>  > >  > is: How can now I extract the raw copy-numbers and the fitted copy-numbers
>  > >  > from the fitted GLAD model "glad"?
>  >
>  > >  For any CopyNumberSegmentationModel (e.g. GladModel and CbsModel), the
>  > >  method getRegions() returns the identified CN regions.  If the
>  > >  segmentation still not have been done for the requested
>  > >  array/chromosome it will be done (fit() is called internally).
>  > >  Example:

>  > >  str(cnrs)
>  > >  List of 1

>  >
>  > /Henrik
>  >
>  >

>  >
>  >
>  > >  > This is what I tried w/o success:

>  > >  Cheers
>  >
>  > >  Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi Bill,
I've posted this to the general aroma.affymetrix group pages so we can
move the discussion there (so please 'reply to all'). If you don't have
an account on the google groups that goes with aroma.affymetrix, please
sign up first for membership with the aroma-affymetrix group (you don't
need a gmail account). Everyone can respond and learn from the same
mistakes and others can spot your problem if I can't.

I'm not entirely sure about your error yet, but a couple of things first.
1) The 'gene-centric' cdf you are using has both gene and exon
information. If you choose mergeGroups=TRUE, you get estimates of the
gene; if you choose mergeGroups=FALSE you get estimates of the
probeset/exon. It does not have gene names, but it does have Ensembl
identifiers, which you can use to look up a gene name.
2) You should not use the code you have below to get the chip effects --
it is WRONG. getData should be considered a developer's function only.
Instead you should use extractDataFrame(ces). For anyone you have worked
with at LBL on this problem, I would appreciate if you passed this
along--I've tried before, but I don't think the right people were in the
audience...
For example:
ces <- getChipEffects(plm);
df <- extractDataFrame(ces,addNames=TRUE);
can substitute for ALL of that code you had (except the write.table).
3) save(plm, file="bcgc_gene_plm.rda") is not needed. There is really
nothing to save there. It's just a 'link' to the saved information on
disk (in the .CEL files).

Now for the main problem, I am not sure that
chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl47,G-Affy" is the right way to do
this, but I'm not sure because things have been updated and improved on
this front.

Try this tried-but-true code:

chipType<-"HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
cdfEnsb<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(paste(chipType,"U-Ensembl47,G-Affy",sep=","))
ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc",chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2") #I
took out the checkChipType=FALSE, but if that gives you an error, put it
back in, but let us see the error just in case...
bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(ds)
csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose)
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
setCdf(csN,cdfEnsb)
plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)

Then tell us where you first see errors.

Best,
Elizabeth

Here is Bill's code because I forgot it in the previous posting.
library(aroma.affymetrix)
ds =
AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc",chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl47,G-Affy",
checkChipType=FALSE)
bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(ds)
csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose)
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
save(plm, file="bcgc_gene_plm.rda")

qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
pdf(file = "bcgc_gene_ Nuse.pdf", width = 40, height=12)
plotNuse(qam)
dev.off()
pdf(file = "bcgc_gene_Rle.pdf", width = 40, height=12)
plotRle(qam)
dev.off()

ces <- getChipEffects(plm);
chipEffectMatrix <- getData(ces, indices=NULL, "intensities")$intensities
cdf <- getCdf(ces);
groupNames <- readCdfGroupNames(cdf$.pathname);
blanks <- which(unlist(lapply(groupNames, function(x){all(x=="")})));
groupNames[blanks] <- names(groupNames)[blanks];
groupNames <- unlist(groupNames);
chipEffectMatrix <- chipEffectMatrix[1:length(groupNames),];
celNames <- paste(getNames(ds),".CEL",sep="");
header <- rbind(celNames, rep("Signal", length(celNames)));
header <- cbind(c("Hybridization REF", "CompositeElement REF"), header);
df <- data.frame(groupNames, chipEffectMatrix);
write.table(header, file="bcgc_gene_norm.txt", sep="\t", quote=FALSE,
row.names=FALSE,
col.names=FALSE);
write.table(df, file="bcgc_gene_norm.txt", sep="\t", quote=FALSE,
append=TRUE,
row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE);

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Mon, Mar 3, 2008 at 5:41 PM, Yue Hu <yuehu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi
>
>
> I am wondering if the low sample number in paired analysis affect the
> quality of result?
>
> Could the result be more reliable If in stead of using only two cancer
> samples to do paired analysis, grouping them with 6 wildtype samples and do
> total copy number analysis?  Also in this way the copy number might be
> estimated directly since wild type tissue normally have two copy for each
> genome region.

I', not sure what you mean by "low sample number", but in paired
analysis you supposedly calculate raw CNs as the log-ratio between a
test sample and a single normal sample.  Thus, there is a lot of noise
in the normal sample that noise will transfer to your raw CNs as well.
 In stead of having a single normal sample as a reference, one can
also consider doing a paired analysis where the reference is the
average of several normal samples.  Non-paired analysis assumes
nothing about the samples other than that the (robust) majority of
them are diploid at any locus.  So, simply speaking, the more samples
you have in your reference when you calculate your raw CNs the more
precise estimates.  If you do paired analysis with one tumor sample
versus another, the you'll only identify regions that differ between
the two.

There is also an issue of normalization; you must have enough samples
so that the normalization does not introduce artificial copy numbers.

All of the above "rule of thumbs" applies to all kind of microarray
analysis, not just copy number analysis.

/Henrik

> GLAD nor the CBS method tries to *call* the "true" underlying copy
> number in {0,1,2,...} copies but only returns a *mean estimate* on the
> continues scale.  GLAD can call regions as loss, normal, or gain

> > genome region.

> I', not sure what you mean by "low sample number", but in paired
> analysis you supposedly calculate raw CNs as the log-ratio between a
> test sample and a single normal sample.  Thus, there is a lot of noise
> in the normal sample that noise will transfer to your raw CNs as well.
>  In stead of having a single normal sample as a reference, one can
> also consider doing a paired analysis where the reference is the
> average of several normal samples.  Non-paired analysis assumes
> nothing about the samples other than that the (robust) majority of
> them are diploid at any locus.  So, simply speaking, the more samples
> you have in your reference when you calculate your raw CNs the more
> precise estimates.  If you do paired analysis with one tumor sample
> versus another, the you'll only identify regions that differ between
> the two.

> There is also an issue of normalization; you must have enough samples
> so that the normalization does not introduce artificial copy numbers.

> analysis, not just copy number analysis.

On Mon, Mar 3, 2008 at 9:25 PM, Yue Hu <yuehu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,

> I have a naive question: how to make a file that is average of several
> samples?

Assume you have a ChipEffectSet that contains the arrays you want to
average over, then call getAverageFile().  For instance,

# Assume you have preprocessed all your samples together
ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm);

# Use arrays 5 to 15 of this set to calculate the average
cesRef <- extract(ces, 5:15);

# Calculate the average of these 11 files and return an AffymetrixCelFile
ceRef <- getAverageFile(cesRef);

# Say, treat the rest of the arrays as a set of test samples
cesTest <- extract(ces, -(5:15));

You can then use 'ceRef' as a reference array for all test samples
(see paired analysis).

/Henrik

associated R session. By the way, two earlier emails between Elizabeth
and me were merged into one, yielding a somewhat misleading topic name
for this thread. The topic might be better named "a question about
estimating gene expression based on exon array data."

Here is the initial environment:

CDF file:
  exon/annotationData/chipTypes/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-
Ensembl47,G-Affy.cdf

---------------

> ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc",chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2")

Error in list("AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc", chipType = "HuEx-1_0-

[2008-03-03 23:37:32] Exception: Could not create AffymetrixCdfFile
object. No CDF file with that chip type found: HuEx-1_0-st-v2

---------------

AROMA seems to want the name of the CEL files directory to match the
name of the CDF file. Wanting to keep the nature of the CDF file
clearly labeled, I changed the name of the CEL files directory to:

  exon/rawData/bcgc/HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl47,G-Affy

Re-running, I get a different error message:

---------------

> ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc",chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl47,G-Affy")
Error in list("AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc", chipType = "HuEx-1_0-

No errors, however I am wondering whether it is correct to append U-
Ensembl47,G-Affy to the chipType string.

getChipEffects, new errors surface:

---------------

Error in list("plotNuse(qam)" = <environment>,

Error in UseMethod("extractDataFrame") :

Bill

>

> First of all, note that the log-ratio scale has *not* been calibrated
> to be linear with the true underlying copy number.  This is because we
> do not have a way to do this calibration in a random data set.  The
> only thing done is to rescale the CNs across arrays such that diploid
> loci are likely to have log-ratio 0.

> Second, as a wrote in a different thread on a related question,

> assumptions such as homogenuous cells and so on.  This is the reason

>

>  Ensembl47,G-Affy.cdf

>

>  Error in list("AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc", chipType = "HuEx-1_0-
>  st-v2")" = <environment>,  :
>  [2008-03-03 23:37:32] Exception: Could not create AffymetrixCdfFile
>  object. No CDF file with that chip type found: HuEx-1_0-st-v2

I suspect that you use the incorrect working directory.  You should be
in the exon/ directory, not in the parent of it.  aroma.affymetrix
needs to see annotationData/, rawData/ and so on in the current
directory, cf. thread 'problems with annotation file directory path'
on 2008-02-05 and especially my troubleshooting "script".

You know that it works if the CDF can be found by:

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HuEx-1_0-st-v2",
tags="U-Ensembl47,G-Affy");
print(cdf);

>
>  ---------------
>
>  AROMA seems to want the name of the CEL files directory to match the
>  name of the CDF file. Wanting to keep the nature of the CDF file
>  clearly labeled, I changed the name of the CEL files directory to:
>
>   exon/rawData/bcgc/HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl47,G-Affy

No, you do not want this.  The 'chip type' is not the same as the
'CDF'.  One 'chip type' can have many different CDFs, but one CDF
belongs to only one chip type.  The chip type is what comes out of the
Affymetrix factory and will never change, but the CDF may get updated
over time and custom CDFs can be created. [Unfortunately there are
quite a few Bioconductor packages that have blurred the distinction
between chip types and CDFs over the years].

So, the subdirectory of your data set 'bcgc', should be the name of
the 'chip type' and nothing else.

After grabbing the CDF as above, you can setup your data set by:

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("bcgc", cdf=cdf);
print(cs);

Please see the online Vignette 'Human exon array analysis'
illustrating exactly this.

I'll leave the below issues as is and if they reoccur, which they
might, please repost.

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Tue, Mar 4, 2008 at 1:12 AM, cstratowa
<Christian...@vie.boehringer-ingelheim.com> wrote:
>
>  Dear Henrik
>
>  Thank you.
>
>
>  On Mar 3, 6:52 pm, "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
>  > Hi.
>  >
>  > On Mon, Mar 3, 2008 at 3:50 AM, cstratowa
>  >
>
> > <Christian.Strat...@vie.boehringer-ingelheim.com> wrote:
>  >
>  > >  Dear Henrik
>  >
>
> > >  Thank you for your detailed reply, getRegions() was the method I was
>  > >  looking for.
>  >
>  > >  The method writeRegions() is also very convenient, since it exports
>  > >  the results as an Excel-file:
>  >
>  > It is not really an Excel file but a tab-delimited file with file
>  > extension *.xls for easy opening in Excel (inspired by how dChip does
>  > it).
>  >
>  > >  However, running your example:
>  >
>  > > > pathname <- writeRegions(glad, arrays=1, chromosomes=1:4, organism="Human", hgVersion="hg18")
>  > >  and opening the Excel-file I realized that the Excel-file contains
>  > >  already data for all arrays and all chromosomes,
>  > >  and added the new results at the end. It seems that I did already have
>  > >  this Excel-file and new data are always appended.
>  > >  Is this corect?
>  >
>  > I guess that is the current behavior.  writeRegions() is also called
>  > everything you do process() via the ChromosomeExplorer.  I guess that
>  > is what you've done and the reason for why you already got results.
>  > For safety, I guess I decided to append data rather than overwriting
>  > it.
>  >
>  Yes I did do process() via chromosome explorer, so this explains the
>  appended data.
>
>
>  >
>  >
>  > >  Furthermore, I get the following result for one region:
>  > >         mean    count call
>  > >         -4.402  5       loss
>  > >  I suppose, that 'mean' is the log2ratio of the mean raw CN levels,
>  > >  e.g. log2(0.1/2)=-4.32, thus mean CN=0.
>  >
>  > First of all, note that the log-ratio scale has *not* been calibrated
>  > to be linear with the true underlying copy number.  This is because we
>  > do not have a way to do this calibration in a random data set.  The
>  > only thing done is to rescale the CNs across arrays such that diploid
>  > loci are likely to have log-ratio 0.
>  >
>  > Second, as a wrote in a different thread on a related question,
>  > *calling* copy numbers {0,1,2,...} is much harder and relies on more
>  > assumptions such as homogenuous cells and so on.  This is the reason
>  > why the CN is reported on the continuous scale.  GLAD tries to
>  > classify regions as loss, normal, and gain, but it is done in an "ad
>  > hoc" way so you should rely on those calls blindly.
>  >
>  >
>  >
>  > >  Although you mention that getRawCnData() is not a public method, I am
>  > >  curious:
>  > >  How do I get (a list of) ChipEffectFiles?
>  >
>  > If you get the ChipEffectSet, which you pass to the segmentation
>  > model, then you get the files as list by calling getFiles().  [There
>  > is also as.list() but I'm not sure if that is a good name to be kept.]
>  >
>  >
>  So, in principle I could extract ceList and refList from getFile(ces)
>  and use these in function getRawCnData().

Yes.

>
>
> >
>  >
>  > >  Finally, please allow me to make a comment, since getRegions() is a
>  > >  good example of my problems:
>  > >  Since most methods are not explained in the help file, I need to look
>  > >  at the source code, e.g.file CopyNumberSegmentationModel.R:
>  >
>  > >  - setMethodS3("getRegions", "CopyNumberSegmentationModel",
>  > >  function(this, ..., url="ucsc", organism="Human", hgVersion="hg17",
>  > >  margin=10, flat=FALSE, verbose=FALSE)
>  > >  is not documented, and there is no hint that I can pass parameters
>  > >  arrays and chromosomes to this method. Thus I could not see that this
>  > >  method would be the one I need.
>  >
>  > >  In contrast,
>  > >  -  setMethodS3("fit", "CopyNumberSegmentationModel", function(this,
>  > >  arrays=NULL, chromosomes=getChromosomes(this),
>  > >  force=FALSE, ..., .retResults=FALSE, verbose=FALSE)
>  > >  is documented and shows that I need parameters arrays and chromosomes.
>  >
>  > For maintainance and quality reasons I try to keep code redundancy to
>  > a minimal.  This will also minimize the risk for having the same bug
>  > in multiple places.  One way to to minimize redundancy is to pass
>  > arguments handled by other methods via '...'.  I do try to write in
>  > the Rd help where '...' is passed to so one can follow the arguments a
>  > bit easier.  Although, it is not unlikely that there are places where
>  > code have changed but the docs lag behind.
>  >
>  >
>  >
>  > >  Since there are hundreds of methods it would be helpful to know which
>  > >  methods are public and which ones are private (i.e. for internal use
>  > >  only). Furthermore, it would be helpful if the public methods would be
>  > >  explained in help files.
>  >
>  > Sure indeed.  However, last time I checked (April 2007) the source
>  > code and the Rd files filled almost one thousand (=963) pages.  There
>  > is basically no chance/time for me to keep everything up to date.
>  >
>  > Someone ones said "who needs documentation when you've got code".  I
>  > guess it applies here.  To be more serious, you probably should trust
>  > the code to be more up to date than the Rd help.  What you can trust
>  > in the Rd help is that the usage, the list of arguments are correct
>  > and example code, because that is validated while building the
>  > package.
>  >
>  > So the strategy I use instead is that what is documented on the group
>  > pages show the part of the API that you can expect to be rather stable
>  > and be around for a while.
>  >
>  > Via the R.oo framework I also "tag" methods as private, protected, and
>  > public.  Example:
>  >
>  > > methods("getRegions")
>  >
>  > [1] getRegions.CopyNumberSegmentationModel
>  > [2] getRegions.profileCGH> attributes(getRegions.profileCGH)
>  >
>  > $modifiers
>  > [1] "private"> attributes(getRegions.CopyNumberSegmentationModel)
>  >
>  > $modifiers
>  > [1] "public"
>  >
>  > These tags are not really up to date all the time, because if not
>  > specified explicitly in the code they default to "public".  However,
>  > whenever you see a "private" or "protected" tag, you should be careful
>  > using it in your code without asking first.  Consider them as internal
>  > support functions of aroma.affymetrix that have their own life.  If
>  > aroma.affymetrix ever get a namespace, the private methods are the
>  > first ones to "disappear" (=not be exported).
>  >
>  I understand, at least methods() will help me identify the public
>  methods.

As outlined above, yes, but *not* by looking for "sealed" methods with
asterisks, e.g.

> methods("boxplot")
[1] boxplot.default  boxplot.formula*

Those only apply for package with namespaces and aroma.affymetrix does
not have one at this stage.

/Henrik

>
>
>
>  > Having said all this, contributions/corrections are welcome and appreciated.
>  >
>  > Cheers
>  >
>  > Henrik
>  >
>  Best regards
>  Christian

>  >

>  > >  > >  > the (relative) copy-numbers.
>  >

>  > >  > >  > > cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chiptypes[1])

>  > >  > >  > # correct for allelic cross talk

>  Hi Henrik,
>
>  (1) I only have snp probesets on my custom array, should I use
>  RmaCnPlm()?

Sure. There is also AvgCnPlm() that can be used if the probes are
technical replicates (as in GWS5 and GWS6).  The latter is a
single-array summarization method and our current results indicate
that the RmaCnPlm() is slightly better; we don't know the exact reason
for, maybe it is because the estimates are more robust.

>  (2) is there a way to output the chip effect (ces) or allocate them in
>  a matrix? We want to implement a different way of specifiying
>  reference and then run R/DNAcopy for segmentation.

See the Vignette 'Calculating raw total copy numbers manually'
illustrating how to use extractMatrix().  In the latest version there
is also extractDataFrame(), e.g.

data <- extractDataFrame(ces, units=1000:1100, addNames=TRUE)
print(data[1:5,1:7])

Error in list("AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc", chipType = "HuEx-1_0-
st-v2")" = <environment>,  :

[2008-03-04 22:17:50] Exception: Could not create AffymetrixCdfFile

$byName method. That worked fine, without errors:

It seems that the original problem stems from the use of the $fromName
method.

[2008-03-04 22:59:45] Exception: The specified CDF structure is not

332929 != 233289

(a) replace the gene-centric HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl47,G-Affy.cdf
with the exon-centric HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.cdf, and

Bill

chipType=chiptype, verbose=verbose);
      csList[[chiptype]] <- cs;

"normalizeData.AromaSNP" <-
function(object, verbose = FALSE, ...) {

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

 I'm posting this one back to the mailing list.  FYI, I block replies
 to some of my message such as update announcements on purpose.  This
 way "sticky" announcements are easy to read on the online Discussion
 page.

 On Wed, Mar 5, 2008 at 1:51 AM, cstratowa
 <Christian.Str...@...> wrote:
 > Dear Henrik
 >
 >  Since I need to download packages first and install them locally,
 >  could you please
 >  mention next time the packages which need to be updated in addition to
 >  aroma.affymetrix.
 >
 >  When I updated only aroma.affymetrix to 0.9.0 everything was ok.

 In any package there is a DESCRIPTION file, which specifies the
 dependencies of other package which optionally can also include
 package versions.  I specify package versions in all my packages where
 I know the version makes a difference.  Thus, by looking at
 DESCRIPTION of aroma.affymetrix you can see what packages you have to
 update.

 Actually, since the aroma.affymetrix v0.9.0 was quite a big update, I
 (think I) avoided updating other packages at the same time.  This way
 it would be easier to locate bugs.  In other words, I don't think
 other packages had to be updated (although updates are available).

 I'm not sure if 'library(aroma.affymetrix)' or 'R CMD INSTALL
 aroma.affymetrix' will complain if you don't have the right
 dependencies, but 'R CMD check aroma.affymetrix' would for sure.

 >  However, currently
 >  I am writing my own package which depends on aroma.affymetrix.
 >  Although I can
 >  install my package w/o problems, when I did "R CMD check mypkg",
 >  checking examples
 >  resulted in following error:
 >  Error in match(x, table, nomatch = 0) :
 >   formal argument "nomatch" matched by multiple actual arguments
 >  Error: package/namespace load failed for 'mysnp'
 >  Execution halted
 >
 >  Only after updating R.utils and R.cache, too, this error disappeared.
 >  Thus it would be great to have this information when you announce your
 >  next update.

 I'm not sure what went wrong here.  It might have to do with how
 setMethodS3() of R.methodsS3 "hardwires" method definitions of other
 package upon installation and that over time they have to be updated
 when R get updated.  ...heard the following before? ;)  What's you
 sessionInfo()?

 Cheers

 Henrik

 >
 >  Thank you in advance.
 >  Christian

that is used is good old S3 methods.

>  2, Since the error occurs in "process(acc, verbose=verbose)": Is there
>  any information missing,
>  which I need to supply so that the genome information is found?

Yes, the error message looks for "genome information" annotation data,
because now the default in AllelicCrosstalkCalibration is to exclude
data points on ChrX & ChrY.  Did you try the same code without
wrapping it up?

In order to infer what probes are on what chromosome extra annotation
data is needed.  The term "genome information" is the working term
inherited from dChip and the fact that aroma.affymetrix used (and can
still use) dChip's so called "genome information annotation files".
We are now moving towards using UGP files instead, so just make sure
the package can find the corresponding one and everything should be
find.  Alternatively you can fit the model using all data points by
using argument 'subsetToAvg=NULL' in AllelicCrosstalkCalibration.

>  compatible with the CEL file. The number of cells do not match:
>  332929 != 233289
>  -----------------------------

Did you fit a PLM previously using a different CDF?  It might be that
there already are a set of fitted chip effect files for this other CDF
and now it clashes.  If so, I would expect that you get the same error
if you don't call fit() but instead:

  ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)

You could try to add another tag when you setup the PLM in order to
get a "fresh run", e.g.

plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE, tags="*,Ensemble");
ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm);
fit(plm, verbose=verbose);

Does that work?

>  $fromName("bcgc", cdf=cdfEnsb) method.

fromName() and byName() do the same thing.  It all used to be
fromName(), but I think byName() sounds better so I'm slowly migrating
the package to use that.  Same with fromChipType() and byChipType().
Feedback on this is appreciated.

Cheers

/Henrik

Henrik's suggestion about adding the tags sounds very likely. I just had
a couple of small comments about some things you said that are more FYI
than addressing your problem (sorry!).

>> ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc",chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2")

This error is because it is looking by default for a cdf called
'HuEx-1_0-st-v2.cdf'; this is usually reserved for the (unsupported) cdf
put out by Affy and it is probeset specific -- each unit has 1 group
(well, almost) and corresponds to a probeset (exon). So probably you
just don't have that in your directory. It's not necessary, but
originally I think it was; Henrik has updated the code to allow you to
bypass that.

The 'HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.cdf' is not 'exon specific'. It has 'genes'
that are Affy's transcript cluster's; the 'core' refers to the fact that
it only contains the 'core' probesets, but it *is* organized by
transcript cluster (gene). The only cdf that is exon specific is Affy's.
The transcript cluster's are Affy's clustering of exons to get something
like a gene model. I think that if you are only interested in 'reliable'
probesets then the Ensembl cdf is better (and also not interested in
specific probesets that may not be included). If you want to extend to
other probesets then you need to use Affy's transcript clusters.

Furthermore, 'HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.cdf' is outdated. It comes from older
annotation and also has some problems as to some of the
probeset/transcript cluster definitions. I don't remember the details,
but I do remember that it assigns some probes to more than 1
gene/transcript cluster, which is biologically possible but Affy's
transcript clusters do not have this property so this is an error. Also,
the plm can't isn't expecting this, so things like residuals and weights
will be wrong for those probes. There are updated versions of these cdfs
on the group pages.

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.body_plain:
Hmm... that one took a while to figure out because I could not
reproduce it on either Windows on Linux, but I found and old R v2.5.1
on OSX where I got the same error and could fix it (details below for
the record).  I learned something today.

I've uploaded a patch which (I hope) solves the problem.  Install and
apply the patch by:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

If you then can do the following without errors, you should be able to
build you UGP file:

> xmlToList(listToXml(list(a=2)))
$a
[1] "2"

Let us know if it helps.

DETAILS:  The reason is probably obvious when you know it and know a
bit of ASCII, about locales etc.  This is what I learned:

> regexpr("[a-Z]", "foo")
Error in regexpr(pattern, text, extended, fixed, useBytes) :
        invalid regular expression '[a-Z]'
> regexpr("[a-zA-Z]", "foo")
[1] 1
attr(,"match.length")
[1] 1
> regexpr("[A-z]", "foo")
[1] 1
attr(,"match.length")
[1] 1

In ASCII, the upper-case letters comes before the lower-case ones, and
for some reason does the native regexpr complain about pattern 'a-Z',
which have to be 'A-z'.  On Windows and Linux this is more forgiving.

Cheers

/Henrik

On Thu, Mar 6, 2008 at 7:08 AM, JP <playb...@yahoo.com> wrote:
>
>  plm <- RmaCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=
>  +300)
>
>  When I type help(RmaCnPlm), it only explain combineAlleles.

'mergeStrands' is passed via '...' to superclass RmaSnpPlm where it is
documented (if you look at the HTML help pages it is easier to
navigate between these help pages).  It means, fit the model ignoring
information about 'strands' (as if all probes were on the same
strand).

'shift' is also passed via '...' to RmaSnpPlm to RmaPlm to
ProbeLevelModel, where it is documented.

>
>  What does the shif parameter concerns? How does the mergeStrands
>  work?

It translates each probe signal with that amount, shift=300 adds 300
to each signal (on the intensity scale) before fitting the model.

>
>  How to find more information about the arguments of a function besides
>  using help()?

Online documentation/examples ...and source code.

overwhelming task to document all bits and details, and then to keep
it up to date, but at least I try to avoid errors.

messages.subject_clean: comparison of Affymetrix data from cartridge and HT arrays
messages.body_plain:
Henrik, Elizabeth,

Adding tags did the trick. Thank you very kindly for your patience and
guidance.

For reference, here is the version of the script that worked for me. I
included getChipEffects() in two places: just before fit() (per
Henrik's suggestion) and just before extractDataFrame(). Is it
necessary to call getChipEffects() prior to calling fit()? Would
inclusion of tag=",*Ensemble" be sufficient to signal a "fresh run?"

Regards,

Bill

------------------------------------------

library(aroma.affymetrix)

chipType<-"HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
cdfEnsb <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType, tags="U-
Ensembl47,G-Affy")
ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("bcgc", cdf=cdfEnsb);

bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(ds)
csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose)
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
setCdf(csN,cdfEnsb)

plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE, tags="*,Ensemble")

ces <- getChipEffects(plm);
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)

qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
pdf(file = "bcgc_gene_Nuse.pdf", width = 40, height=12)
plotNuse(qam)

dev.off()
pdf(file = "bcgc_gene_Rle.pdf", width = 40, height=12)
plotRle(qam)
dev.off()

ces <- getChipEffects(plm);

df <- extractDataFrame(ces,addNames=TRUE);

write.table(header, file="bcgc_gene_norm.txt", sep="\t", quote=FALSE,
row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE);
write.table(df, file="bcgc_gene_norm.txt", sep="\t", quote=FALSE,
append=TRUE, row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE);

------------------------------------------

On Mar 5, 3:03 pm, Elizabeth Purdom <epur...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Bill,
>
> Henrik's suggestion about adding the tags sounds very likely. I just had
> a couple of small comments about some things you said that are more FYI
> than addressing your problem (sorry!).
>
> >> ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc",chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2")
>
> > Error in list("AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc", chipType = "HuEx-1_0-
> > st-v2")" = <environment>,  :
> > [2008-03-03 23:37:32] Exception: Could not create AffymetrixCdfFile
> > object. No CDF file with that chip type found: HuEx-1_0-st-v2
>
> This error is because it is looking by default for a cdf called
> 'HuEx-1_0-st-v2.cdf'; this is usually reserved for the (unsupported) cdf
> put out by Affy and it is probeset specific -- each unit has 1 group
> (well, almost) and corresponds to a probeset (exon). So probably you
> just don't have that in your directory. It's not necessary, but
> originally I think it was; Henrik has updated the code to allow you to
> bypass that.
>
> The 'HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.cdf' is not 'exon specific'. It has 'genes'
> that are Affy's transcript cluster's; the 'core' refers to the fact that
> it only contains the 'core' probesets, but it *is* organized by
> transcript cluster (gene). The only cdf that is exon specific is Affy's.
> The transcript cluster's are Affy's clustering of exons to get something
> like a gene model. I think that if you are only interested in 'reliable'
> probesets then the Ensembl cdf is better (and also not interested in
> specific probesets that may not be included). If you want to extend to
> other probesets then you need to use Affy's transcript clusters.
>
> Furthermore, 'HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.cdf' is outdated. It comes from older
> annotation and also has some problems as to some of the
> probeset/transcript cluster definitions. I don't remember the details,
> but I do remember that it assigns some probes to more than 1
> gene/transcript cluster, which is biologically possible but Affy's
> transcript clusters do not have this property so this is an error. Also,
> the plm can't isn't expecting this, so things like residuals and weights
> will be wrong for those probes. There are updated versions of these cdfs
> on the group pages.
>
> Best,
> Elizabeth

>  included getChipEffects() in two places: just before fit() (per
>  Henrik's suggestion) and just before extractDataFrame(). Is it
>  necessary to call getChipEffects() prior to calling fit()?

A minor comment: In an effort of making method names more consistent,
getChipEffectSet() is prefer over getChipEffects() - the latter call
the former so they work the same.

No, you don't have to call getChipEffectSet() before calling fit(),
that is done internally in fit() anyway.  I only suggested that in
order to out rule that the error may have occured in fit().

>  Would inclusion of tag=",*Ensemble" be sufficient to signal a "fresh run?"

That's tag="*,Ensemble".  The tag(s) will be part of the pathname to
make the output/result data set unique on the file system.  The
asterisk ('*') tag is expanded with the default tags according to the
model/method class including special parameter settings.  By adding
'Ensemble' that tag will also be part of the pathname, but there is
nothing magic about the sequence "Ensemble".

So, each time you add a tag that hasn't been used before, then yes,
you will get a "fresh run".    If you use the same tag(s) again for
the same setup, aroma.affymetrix will locate that output data set and
work with it.

/Henrik

>
>  Regards,
>
>  Bill
>
>  ------------------------------------------
>
>  library(aroma.affymetrix)
>
>
>  chipType<-"HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
>
> cdfEnsb <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType, tags="U-
>  Ensembl47,G-Affy")
>
> ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("bcgc", cdf=cdfEnsb);
>
> bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(ds)
>  csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose)
>  qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
>  csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
>  setCdf(csN,cdfEnsb)
>  plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE, tags="*,Ensemble")
>  ces <- getChipEffects(plm);
>  fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
>
>
>  qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
>  pdf(file = "bcgc_gene_Nuse.pdf", width = 40, height=12)
>  plotNuse(qam)
>  dev.off()
>  pdf(file = "bcgc_gene_Rle.pdf", width = 40, height=12)
>  plotRle(qam)
>  dev.off()
>
>  ces <- getChipEffects(plm);
>
> df <- extractDataFrame(ces,addNames=TRUE);
>
>
> write.table(header, file="bcgc_gene_norm.txt", sep="\t", quote=FALSE,
>  row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE);
>  write.table(df, file="bcgc_gene_norm.txt", sep="\t", quote=FALSE,
>  append=TRUE, row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE);
>
>  ------------------------------------------
>
>
>
>
>  On Mar 5, 3:03 pm, Elizabeth Purdom <epur...@gmail.com> wrote:
>  > Hi Bill,
>  >
>  > Henrik's suggestion about adding the tags sounds very likely. I just had
>  > a couple of small comments about some things you said that are more FYI
>  > than addressing your problem (sorry!).
>  >
>  > >> ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc",chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2")
>  >
>  > > Error in list("AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("bcgc", chipType = "HuEx-1_0-
>  > > st-v2")" = <environment>,  :
>  > > [2008-03-03 23:37:32] Exception: Could not create AffymetrixCdfFile
>  > > object. No CDF file with that chip type found: HuEx-1_0-st-v2
>  >
>  > This error is because it is looking by default for a cdf called
>  > 'HuEx-1_0-st-v2.cdf'; this is usually reserved for the (unsupported) cdf
>  > put out by Affy and it is probeset specific -- each unit has 1 group
>  > (well, almost) and corresponds to a probeset (exon). So probably you
>  > just don't have that in your directory. It's not necessary, but
>  > originally I think it was; Henrik has updated the code to allow you to
>  > bypass that.
>  >
>  > The 'HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.cdf' is not 'exon specific'. It has 'genes'
>  > that are Affy's transcript cluster's; the 'core' refers to the fact that
>  > it only contains the 'core' probesets, but it *is* organized by
>  > transcript cluster (gene). The only cdf that is exon specific is Affy's.
>  > The transcript cluster's are Affy's clustering of exons to get something
>  > like a gene model. I think that if you are only interested in 'reliable'
>  > probesets then the Ensembl cdf is better (and also not interested in
>  > specific probesets that may not be included). If you want to extend to
>  > other probesets then you need to use Affy's transcript clusters.
>  >
>  > Furthermore, 'HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.cdf' is outdated. It comes from older
>  > annotation and also has some problems as to some of the
>  > probeset/transcript cluster definitions. I don't remember the details,
>  > but I do remember that it assigns some probes to more than 1
>  > gene/transcript cluster, which is biologically possible but Affy's
>  > transcript clusters do not have this property so this is an error. Also,
>  > the plm can't isn't expecting this, so things like residuals and weights
>  > will be wrong for those probes. There are updated versions of these cdfs
>  > on the group pages.
>  >
>  > Best,
>  > Elizabeth
>  >
>

custom array and if so could you post the solution?

> On Tue, Mar 4, 2008 at 11:24 AM, JP <playboat...@yahoo.com> wrote:

>
> >  (1) I only have snp probesets on my custom array, should I use
> >  RmaCnPlm()?
>
> Sure. There is also AvgCnPlm() that can be used if the probes are
> technical replicates (as in GWS5 and GWS6).  The latter is a
> single-array summarization method and our current results indicate
> that the RmaCnPlm() is slightly better; we don't know the exact reason
> for, maybe it is because the estimates are more robust.
>
> >  (2) is there a way to output the chip effect (ces) or allocate them in
> >  a matrix? We want to implement a different way of specifiying
> >  reference and then run R/DNAcopy for segmentation.
>
> See the Vignette 'Calculating raw total copy numbers manually'
> illustrating how to use extractMatrix().  In the latest version there
> is also extractDataFrame(), e.g.
>
> data <- extractDataFrame(ces, units=1000:1100, addNames=TRUE)
> print(data[1:5,1:7])
> ##        unitName groupName unit group cell   NA06985  NA06991

> I'm not sure what part of the ChromosomeExplorer you refer to.  If you
> ignore the cytobands which are the ones specified by the GLAD package

> "Mapping250K_Sty".

On purpose, because should it return the chip type of the (input) data set or the (output) result set?  This makes a difference if you ask for the "fullname" chip type (e.g. including the "monocell" tag).  Instead do:

ds <- getDataSet(plm)
getChipType(ds)

and

ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
getChipType(ces)

and there is no double what you get.  The one you see in the output, is the chip type for the data set (the former).

/Henrik

there are several issues below, so I'm first giving you the summary
what you need to do and then I'll explain where your mistakes are.

This is what you need to do:

(1) Update aroma.affymetrix. Your version is not the latest one.  See
instructions online. Always use the latest version (as the message
footer says below).
(2) Read up on how to setup your annotationData/ and rawData/
directories.  See instructions online.
(3) Read the the vignettes and try to follow the general method calls
as close as possible.  Some parts don't apply, but at least try to
avoid introducing your own solutions and avoid trial-and-error
solutions.
(4) If your code is inspired by some example online, *please* let me
know so it can be corrected/removed.

If you do the above, I'm sure we can get it to work for you and you'll
also avoid future mishaps.

This is not correct (=wrong).  Rule #1 when using aroma.affymetrix is
that you should never ever have to specify an absolute pathname, e.g.
"~/annotationData/...".  If you have code that does that, that is a
strong indication you're on the wrong trail.  Instead, use the
AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType() construct.  See examples online.

Also incorrect. Use the AffymetrixCelSet$fromName() construct.  See

'Installation, Updates & Patches' page how to do this.

Those calls returns what you ask for, you get intensities for cell

messages.body_plain:
Hi Aroma Affymetrix list,

I am working with aroma.affymetrix and am trying to extract the unit
intensities from an AffymetrixCelSet for a particular unit. I am only
interested in the perfect match probes at this stage so I used:

getUnitIntensities(cs, units = 26, stratifyBy = "pm")

but it gave me all the probes, mismatch included.

I believe this is caused by the ... argument not being passed to
readUnits at line 927 of AffymetrixCelSet.R (aroma.affymetrix 0.9.0).

I can get around it by using:

cdf <- readUnits(getCdf(cs), units=26, stratifyBy = "pm")
getUnitIntensities(cs, units = cdf)

but I think it would be cleaner if I could just use stratifyBy in
getUnitIntensities.

If I am going about this the wrong way, please let me know.

Cheers,
Tim Keighley

Hi Tim,

On Tue, Mar 11, 2008 at 3:24 PM,  <Tim.Ke...@csiro.au> wrote:
>
>  Hi Aroma Affymetrix list,
>
>  I am working with aroma.affymetrix and am trying to extract the unit
>  intensities from an AffymetrixCelSet for a particular unit. I am only
>  interested in the perfect match probes at this stage so I used:
>
>  getUnitIntensities(cs, units = 26, stratifyBy = "pm")
>
>  but it gave me all the probes, mismatch included.
>
>  I believe this is caused by the ... argument not being passed to
>  readUnits at line 927 of AffymetrixCelSet.R (aroma.affymetrix 0.9.0).

Correct.  Thanks for reporting this.  I've fixed this for the next
version.  In the meanwhile patches are available.

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

Patches are currently store in the global environment, so if you clean
that out, you have to call the following to reapply the patches:

patchPackage("aroma.affymetrix");

Then you get:

cdf <- getCdf(cs);
units <- 26:31;
for (stratifyBy in c("pm", "mm", "pmmm")) {
  cdfUnits <- readUnits(cdf, units=units, stratifyBy=stratifyBy);
  y1 <- readUnits(cs, units=cdfUnits);
  y2 <- getUnitIntensities(cs, units=units, stratifyBy=stratifyBy);
  stopifnot(identical(y1,y2));
}
print("ok");

By fixing this mishaps I also found a cache-bug in readUnits() of
AffymetrixCelSet causing it to return the same value in the successive
calls if 'cdfUnits' was created for the identical set of units but
with different 'stratifyBy' values.  A very rare scenario, but should
not have happened.

Cheers

Henrik

>   argument "units" is missing, with no default
>
>  If units = NULL is specified it works:
>
>  > readUnits(AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("Mapping50K_Xba240"), units =
>  NULL)
>  ## lots of output

That's correct.  The reason for not have 'units' to default to 'NULL'
was probably to avoid the user to pull out *all* data of a CDF (takes
some time for big CDFs) by mistake and if really wanted one had to
specify 'units=NULL'.  However, the package is not consistent on this
rule, so I made 'units=NULL' the default.

Patches committed.

>
>  Is there any particular reason that readCdfUnits() is called using
>  doCall and not directly? The direct call is in the code but commented
>  out (lines 992:993 AffymetrixCdfFile.R, aroma.affymetrix 0.9.0). Another
>  option is to specify the default units = NULL argument in the function
>  definition.

doCall() is somewhat clever (although not perfect) in removing
arguments in '...' that does not apply to the underlying functions.
It was added because there exist at least one calling function that
passes '...' to readUnits() of AffymetrixCdfFile *as well* as to
acompletely different function.  I left the commented line there as a
reminder for what doCall() is trying to achieve.

Cheers

Henrik

~/.Rpatches/aroma.affymetrix/patches/aroma.affymetrix/<patch date>/.
I've updated the online 'Installation, Updates & Patches' page on
this.  Thanks for the note.

Ah, do you say that class(cesN) does not contain class
'ParameterCelSet'?  That class was added in v0.9.0 of the package.
Then the above errors make sense.   So, you have stored the actual
'cesN' *object* to file and read it back again, or similar, correct?

So, if you take the whole script you've got and rerun it,
aroma.affymetrix detects that each of the steps have been processed
and skips them as it goes.  This is fairly fast (unless you've got
1,000 of arrays).  In other words, you can get a "fresh" 'cesN' by
rerunning your script.  That is pretty much what I do all the time.
Alternatively, you can load the results explicitly like:

cesN <- CnChipEffectSet$byName(dataSet, tags=tags, chipType=chipType,
mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE)

Note the last two arguments; by if you don't specify them explicitly,
aroma.affymetrix has to infer them from reading *all* of the first
result file, which takes an unnecessary long time do to.   [It is on
the to do list to figure out how to store these parameters in the CEL
headers of the result files].

/Henrik

>  > Explanation: all segmentation models in aroma.affymetrix can combine
>  > data from multiple chip types.  The working term for a *list* of CEL
>  > sets is a *CEL set tuple*.  For each chip type there is a reference,
>  > either a single file or a set of files.  In the case of a single file,
>  > we still consider the reference as a set of files (the same file
>  > replicated multiple times).  So,

>  > CEL sets).  Since we know there is only one, we extract that one:
>  >
>  >   refSet <- getListOfSets(refTuple)[[1]]

>  Thank you Henrik.
>  Is there an instruction that allows you to generate the reference cel
>  file without doing the segmentation?

See online Vignette 'Calculating Raw Total Copy Numbers Manually'.
Those instructions does not tell you how to deal with XX and XY for
ChrX.  That you have to do yourself.

>  And, is there an instruction that allows you to select a subgroup from
>  the original data set to calculate the reference and then use it to do
>  the segmentation of the whole data set?

The GladModel and the CbsModel can be subseted to fit a single
chromosome (and a single) array, but you cannot subset to a particular
region.

Alternatively, see the above vignette for estimating raw CNs on a
subset.  To run segmentation on those, you have to call the GLAD or
the CBS methods (in the corresponding packages) manually.  That's
beyond the scope of aroma.affymetrix.

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

no there is no simple way to import log-ratios.  Also, the
FrangmentLengthNormalization is operating on the chip effects and not
the log-ratios (of such), cf. our paper Bengtsson H et al. 2008 (see
group page).  This is slightly different from the ideas implemented in
CNAG, which operates on log-ratios.  It is not that hard to manually
fit and correct for deviations in (l_j, M_ij), using say loess() or
smooth.spline() in R, where fragment lengths l_j and log-ratios M_ij
for loci j=1,...,J per sample i.

Cheers

/Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Fri, Mar 14, 2008 at 1:11 PM, vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx

<vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx> wrote:
>
>
>  Henrik Bengtsson escribió:
>
>
> > Hi.
>  >
>  > On Thu, Mar 13, 2008 at 12:25 PM, vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx
>  > <vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx> wrote:
>  >
>  >>  Henrik Bengtsson escribió:
>  >>
>  >>
>  >>
>  >>> Hi Valeria,
>  >>>
>  >>  >
>  >>  > On Feb 19, 2008 12:52 PM, vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx
>  >>  > <vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx> wrote:
>  >>  >
>  >>  >> Hi,
>  >>  >>
>  >>  >> Can someone tell me if it is possible to access the common reference
>  >>  >> file created and used during the cbs method. Is it possible to use it as
>  >>  >> a reference in  an other  data set?
>  >>  >>
>  >>  >
>  >>  > Example:
>  >>  >
>  >>  > seg <- CbsModel(cesFln);
>  >>  > fit(seg, chromosome=22);
>  >>  > refTuple <- getReferenceSetTuple(seg);
>  >>  > refSet <- getListOfSets(refTuple)[[1]];
>  >>  > refFile <- getFile(refSet, 1);
>  >>  > yRef <- getData(refFile, fields="intensities")$intensities;
>  >>  >
>  >>  > The above applies to any segmentation method, e.g. GladModel and CbsModel.
>  >>  >
>  >>  > Explanation: all segmentation models in aroma.affymetrix can combine
>  >>  > data from multiple chip types.  The working term for a *list* of CEL
>  >>  > sets is a *CEL set tuple*.  For each chip type there is a reference,
>  >>  > either a single file or a set of files.  In the case of a single file,
>  >>  > we still consider the reference as a set of files (the same file
>  >>  > replicated multiple times).  So,
>  >>  >
>  >>  >   refTuple <- getReferenceSetTuple(glad)
>  >>  >
>  >>  > first extract the tuple of CEL set references (contains one or more
>  >>  > CEL sets).  Since we know there is only one, we extract that one:
>  >>  >
>  >>  >   refSet <- getListOfSets(refTuple)[[1]]
>  >>  >
>  >>  > This is a (Cn)ChipEffectSet.  In the above case, it contains the same
>  >>  > reference file replicated nbrOfArrays(cesFln) times.  We get this by:
>  >>  >
>  >>  >   refFile <- getFile(refSet, 1)
>  >>  >
>  >>  > This is a (Cn)ChipEffectFile, e.g.
>  >>  >
>  >>  >
>  >>  >> refFile
>  >>  >>
>  >>  > CnChipEffectFile:
>  >>  > Name: .average-intensities-median-mad
>  >>  > Tags: 01ecc75622a8ca3d584335148e1465cd
>  >>  > Pathname: plmData/Jeremy_2007-10k,ACC,-XY,RMA,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY/Mapping10K_Xba142
>  >>  > /.average-intensities-median-mad,01ecc75622a8ca3d584335148e1465cd.CEL
>  >>  > File size: 445.83kB
>  >>  > RAM: 0.01MB
>  >>  > File format: v4 (binary; XDA)
>  >>  > Chip type: Mapping10K_Xba142,monocell
>  >>  > Timestamp: 2008-01-24 20:10:47
>  >>  > Parameters: (probeModel: chr "pm", mergeStrands: logi TRUE, combineAlleles: logi
>  >>  >  TRUE)
>  >>  >
>  >>  > As you see, it is actually a regular CEL file, but hidden away and
>  >>  > with a hashcode part of the filename.
>  >>  >
>  >>  > The best way to get the probe signals is (for now):
>  >>  >
>  >>  >   yRef <- getData(refFile, fields="intensities")$intensities
>  >>  >
>  >>  > Hope this helps
>  >>  >
>  >>  > /Henrik
>  >>  >
>  >>  >
>  >>  >> Thanks!
>  >>  >> Valeria
>  >>  >>
>  >>  >>
>  >>  >
>  >>  > >
>  >>  >
>  >>  >
>  >>  Thank you Henrik.
>  >>  Is there an instruction that allows you to generate the reference cel
>  >>  file without doing the segmentation?
>  >>
>  >
>  > See online Vignette 'Calculating Raw Total Copy Numbers Manually'.
>  > Those instructions does not tell you how to deal with XX and XY for
>  > ChrX.  That you have to do yourself.
>  >
>  >
>  >>  And, is there an instruction that allows you to select a subgroup from
>  >>  the original data set to calculate the reference and then use it to do
>  >>  the segmentation of the whole data set?
>  >>
>  >
>  > The GladModel and the CbsModel can be subseted to fit a single
>  > chromosome (and a single) array, but you cannot subset to a particular
>  > region.
>  >
>  > Alternatively, see the above vignette for estimating raw CNs on a
>  > subset.  To run segmentation on those, you have to call the GLAD or
>  > the CBS methods (in the corresponding packages) manually.  That's
>  > beyond the scope of aroma.affymetrix.
>  >
>  > Hope this helps
>  >
>  > Henrik
>  >
>  >
>  >>
>  >>  >
>  >>
>  >>
>  >
>  > >
>  >
>  >
>  Hi Henrik,
>
>  I think I didn't explain myself last time.
>  What I want to know is if there is a way to select a subset of samples
>  to be the reference set. In other words, Is it possible to obtain the
>  robust average across a subset of samples instead of the robust avarage
>  across all samples? I know a way to do this would be to create a
>  subdirectory in rawData that only contains the subset and from there
>  obtain the reference but is there a more efficient way to do this?

You don't have to do this.  You can grab a subset of the samples/files
from a set using the extract() method and calculate the robust average
of those, e.g.

cesRef <- extract(ces, c(1:3, 8:11, 34));  A CnChipEffectSet
ceRef <- getAverageFile(cesRref);  # A CnChipEffectFile
rm(cesRef);  # Not needed anymore
print(ceRef);

The you want to use 'ceRef' as you reference in your CBS model.
Currently (I think) you have to make that single ceRef file into a set
of (indentical) files of the same size/length as your test set, e.g.

nbrOfArrays <- nbrOfArrays(ces);
cesRef <- rep(list(ceRef), nbrOfArrays);  # Becomes a list of CnChipEffectFile:s
cesRef <- newInstance(ces, cesRef);  # Turn it into a set of same type as 'ces'.

cns <- CbsModel(ces, cesRef);
print(cns);

This is the same idea as when you do paired CN analysis, cf. Vignette
'Paired total copy number analysis'.   Now, this becomes a bit more
complicated if you want to do if for two chip types together, e.g.
Mapping250K_Nsp and Mapping250K_Sty.  If you want that, first try it
with one chip type and get it to work, then get back here.

/Henrik

>
>  Thank you,
>  Valeria
>
>
>
>  >
>

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: reference in cbs method
messages.body_plain:
Henrik Bengtsson escribió:

> Hi.
>
> On Thu, Mar 13, 2008 at 12:25 PM, vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx
> <vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx> wrote:
>
>>  Henrik Bengtsson escribió:
>>
>>
>>
>>> Hi Valeria,
>>>
>>  >
>>  > On Feb 19, 2008 12:52 PM, vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx
>>  > <vesp...@inmegen.gob.mx> wrote:
>>  >
>>  >> Hi,
>>  >>
>>  >> Can someone tell me if it is possible to access the common reference
>>  >> file created and used during the cbs method. Is it possible to use it as
>>  >> a reference in  an other  data set?
>>  >>
>>  >
>>  > Example:
>>  >
>>  > seg <- CbsModel(cesFln);
>>  > fit(seg, chromosome=22);
>>  > refTuple <- getReferenceSetTuple(seg);
>>  > refSet <- getListOfSets(refTuple)[[1]];
>>  > refFile <- getFile(refSet, 1);
>>  > yRef <- getData(refFile, fields="intensities")$intensities;
>>  >
>>  > The above applies to any segmentation method, e.g. GladModel and CbsModel.
>>  >
>>  > Explanation: all segmentation models in aroma.affymetrix can combine
>>  > data from multiple chip types.  The working term for a *list* of CEL
>>  > sets is a *CEL set tuple*.  For each chip type there is a reference,
>>  > either a single file or a set of files.  In the case of a single file,
>>  > we still consider the reference as a set of files (the same file
>>  > replicated multiple times).  So,
>>  >
>>  >   refTuple <- getReferenceSetTuple(glad)
>>  >
>>  > first extract the tuple of CEL set references (contains one or more
>>  > CEL sets).  Since we know there is only one, we extract that one:
>>  >
>>  >   refSet <- getListOfSets(refTuple)[[1]]
>>  >
>>  > This is a (Cn)ChipEffectSet.  In the above case, it contains the same
>>  > reference file replicated nbrOfArrays(cesFln) times.  We get this by:
>>  >
>>  >   refFile <- getFile(refSet, 1)
>>  >
>>  > This is a (Cn)ChipEffectFile, e.g.
>>  >
>>  >
>>  >> refFile
>>  >>
>>  > CnChipEffectFile:
>>  > Name: .average-intensities-median-mad
>>  > Tags: 01ecc75622a8ca3d584335148e1465cd
>>  > Pathname: plmData/Jeremy_2007-10k,ACC,-XY,RMA,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY/Mapping10K_Xba142
>>  > /.average-intensities-median-mad,01ecc75622a8ca3d584335148e1465cd.CEL
>>  > File size: 445.83kB
>>  > RAM: 0.01MB
>>  > File format: v4 (binary; XDA)
>>  > Chip type: Mapping10K_Xba142,monocell
>>  > Timestamp: 2008-01-24 20:10:47
>>  > Parameters: (probeModel: chr "pm", mergeStrands: logi TRUE, combineAlleles: logi
>>  >  TRUE)
>>  >
>>  > As you see, it is actually a regular CEL file, but hidden away and
>>  > with a hashcode part of the filename.
>>  >
>>  > The best way to get the probe signals is (for now):
>>  >
>>  >   yRef <- getData(refFile, fields="intensities")$intensities
>>  >
>>  > Hope this helps
>>  >
>>  > /Henrik
>>  >
>>  >
>>  >> Thanks!
>>  >> Valeria
>>  >>
>>  >>
>>  >
>>  > >
>>  >
>>  >
>>  Thank you Henrik.
>>  Is there an instruction that allows you to generate the reference cel
>>  file without doing the segmentation?
>>
>
> See online Vignette 'Calculating Raw Total Copy Numbers Manually'.
> Those instructions does not tell you how to deal with XX and XY for
> ChrX.  That you have to do yourself.
>
>
>>  And, is there an instruction that allows you to select a subgroup from
>>  the original data set to calculate the reference and then use it to do
>>  the segmentation of the whole data set?
>>
>
> The GladModel and the CbsModel can be subseted to fit a single
> chromosome (and a single) array, but you cannot subset to a particular
> region.
>
> Alternatively, see the above vignette for estimating raw CNs on a
> subset.  To run segmentation on those, you have to call the GLAD or
> the CBS methods (in the corresponding packages) manually.  That's
> beyond the scope of aroma.affymetrix.
>
> Hope this helps
>
> Henrik
>
>
>>
>>  >
>>
>>
>
> >
>
>

Hi Henrik,

I think I didn't explain myself last time.
What I want to know is if there is a way to select a subset of samples
to be the reference set. In other words, Is it possible to obtain the
robust average across a subset of samples instead of the robust avarage
across all samples? I know a way to do this would be to create a
subdirectory in rawData that only contains the subset and from there
obtain the reference but is there a more efficient way to do this?

Thank you,
Valeria

messages.body_plain:
Hi list,

I am writing a fitting procedure which calculates a set of parameters
from a training sample and then applies it to new samples. I generate 6
parameters for each probe. I would like to store these in a convenient
way.

I have been looking at ParameterCel{File|Set} and their subclasses, but
I haven't found any that store more than 2 floats and 1 integer
(corresponding to intensities, stdvs and pixels in the CEL file),
whereas I have 6 floats.

Are there any examples of storing this sort of information? Does it
sound like I am heading in the right direction? Any other suggestions
appreciated.

Cheers,
Tim Keighley

messages.body_plain:
Hi Elizabeth,

The following is the code:

library(aroma.affymetrix)

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
timestampOn(verbose)

#Getting annotation data files
#chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
#cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType, tags="core")
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromFile("HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.cdf")
print(cdf)

# Defining CEL set
#Next we setup the CEL set with the above custom CDF:

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles(".", cdf=cdf)
print(cs)

#Background Adjustment and Normalization
#In order to do RMA background correction, we setup a correction method and runs it by:

bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose)
print(csBC)

#We then setup a quantile normalization method:
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
print(qn)

#and we then run it by:

csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
print(csN)
#This will take approx 30-60s per array.

#Summarization
#To treat transcripts as units, do:
plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
print(plm)

# QC

# To examine NUSE and RLE plots, do
qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
plotNuse(qam)

Hi Gang,
So you are using aroma.affymetrix_0.8.3; this is an old version. There
was a substantial update recently and the new version is 0.9.0. The code
for the NUSE/RLE boxplots was completely rewritten because there was an
error in the code--though not the same as you got, necessarily, but it's
possible that it's related. Certainly all the zeros you are getting are
because of this.

Please update (see instructions on the group pages), try again, and let
us know if that fixes the problem.

The code I sent you to test out will not work without the new version
either, which you may have discovered. You don't need to refit your
previous work since they should be fine.

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

it appears that there is some spam and/or malicious code on one of your sites, check here <http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/averaging-across-array-set?version=8>. You still can read one of the previous versions of this site but since your table of contents <http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web> links there you might want tio change this...

Greetings and thanks for your so far very helpful software,
Frank Ziegner

(University of Tuebingen <http://www.ra.cs.uni-tuebingen.de/>)

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Error with calculateResiduals
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Sat, Mar 15, 2008 at 5:27 AM, Yoshi <Yoshi...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>  All,
>
>  I copied the following lines of codes from Total Copy Number Analysis
>  (10k, 100K, 500K) to learn aroma.affymetrix.  The combineAlleles is
>  set to True in calling RmaCnPlm; however, calculateResiduals gives
>  error with combineAlleles=True.  Following is the errors to show.

Yes, that "error" just tells you that there is no implementation
available for calculating residuals from a PLM fitted with alleles
combined.  The reason for this that before fitting such a PLM, for
SNPs we do PM=PMA+PMB (Bengtsson et al. 2008; online) and the
residuals are for the combined probe signal.  Continuing, we have
decided to store residuals in a regular
CEL file as probe signals, which allows as to use the standard
framework to display the residuals spatially.  The latter is probably
the most common usage of PLM residuals.  With this setup one has to
map the residuals for "PM" above back to the two "PMA" and "PMB"
probes in order to store and display them.  This has not been
implemented.

>  Should I set combineAlleles to FALSE, and what is the effect?  Thanks.

You are going to fit an allele-specific PLM, meaning your residuals
are now per allele.  You have told us what you are going to use the
residuals for, but if it is to look for spatial artifacts, you can
certainly use combineAlleles=FALSE - I do that. The catch is that you
have to refit everything.

/Henrik
