messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Storing multiple parameters in one (or more) CEL files
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Storing multiple parameters in one (or more) CEL files
messages.body_plain:
Hi.

On Tue, Mar 18, 2008 at 12:13 AM,  <Tim.Ke...@csiro.au> wrote:
>
>  Hi list,
>
>  I am writing a fitting procedure which calculates a set of parameters
>  from a training sample and then applies it to new samples. I generate 6
>  parameters for each probe. I would like to store these in a convenient
>  way.
>
>  I have been looking at ParameterCel{File|Set} and their subclasses, but
>  I haven't found any that store more than 2 floats and 1 integer
>  (corresponding to intensities, stdvs and pixels in the CEL file),
>  whereas I have 6 floats.
>
>  Are there any examples of storing this sort of information? Does it
>  sound like I am heading in the right direction? Any other suggestions
>  appreciated.

Yes, we use (binary/XDA) CEL files to store parameter estimates.  They
hold 2 floats and 1 short (in total 4+4+2=10 bytes).  These can be
used to encode/decode anything.  The main rationale we had when we
decided to store estimates in CEL files was that we could utilize the
same framework (affxparser et al, CDF, CEL, ...) for reading and
writing data.  The probe affinities estimates are naturally stored as
a CEL file, since they (in most cases) map one-to-one to probes.  The
chip effects are store in smaller CEL files mapped by the monocell CDF
(which is uniquely defined by the main CDF).

The only way to store more information that 10 bytes per probe is to
use more CEL files.  However, I strongly discourage you from doing
that, mainly because I want to have the leeway for aroma.affymetrix
diverge from the above in a future (a far future) version.

Instead, the easiest way is to just use (R.utils') saveObject() and
loadObject() to store/read parameter estimates.  They work similar to
save()/load() but don't "dump" the object to the global environment.
Try and you'll understand.  I use saveObject()/loadObject() to store
estimates in GladModel/CbsModel; that way I could
postpone/procrastinate/avoid having to define a file format.  The
catch is that you cannot subset on, say, units when reading/writing,
but they are fast and if you want still want to subset by units and
read a lot of arrays, use loadObject() for the first array, then
subset and discard the rest, the loadObject() for next array and so
on.  That is probably good enough and I don't think the I/O will be
too bad.

There was an early decision to stay away from defining new file
formats, mainly because there are already plenty of them out there and
we're not helping out by introducing new ones.  However, for
annotation data such as UGP=(unit, chromosome, position), UFP=(unit,
PCR fragment length) I finally made the decision that we can do better
with binary versions than slow ragged ASCII files.  For this I have
been working on the AromaUnitTabularBinaryFile class - it maps data
indexed by units (as ordered in the CDF).  See
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/aromatabularbinaryfile
for more information.  Note that it is still in an alpha/beta version;
since no one else is using the file format I can modify it and just
provide updated versions of the UGP and UFL files to the users.  When
more people using it, I loose the option and backward compatibility
becomes an issue.  However, I think it is rather flexible right now,
which is why I invite you to have a look at it.   There is no
AromaCellTabularBinaryFile, but there is the superclass
AromaTabularBinaryFile which is more generic.  If you go down this
path, please share your experience with me/others.

Hope this helps

Henrik

>
>  Cheers,
>  Tim Keighley
>

In order for GladModel to identify which arrays that should be couples
from the two chip types, they have to have the same 'name' (as defined
by aroma.affymetrix; see online docs).  They can still have different
'tags'.

>From the above you can see that GladModel thinks there are 60 unique
samples and 30 were hybridized to one chip type and 30 to the other.
I guess this is not what you want.  If it the case that the first 6
digits specifies the sample, you have to rename your fullnames
"1120013" and ""1120014" to have fullnames "112001,3" and "112001,4",
and so on.  That way they get the same names ("112001") and only
differ in tags ("3" and "4").

You can indeed rename your files manually in order to avoid having to
refit everything, but you have to be careful to get it right.  I also
strongly recommend that you rename all your files in rawData/,
probeData/, and plmData/ accordingly; if you do that you should be
able to use the identical script you used now and aroma.affymetrix
will recognize already done work.

Please make sure to read about filename, names, tags, fullnames etc
online; it is very important and extremely useful to understand how
that works.

messages.subject: Re: FIRMA Scores
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I'm pretty new in the 'exon-array-business' so hopefully my questions
won't be too stupid...

I'm using your software for some weeks now trying to get some
information about alternative splicing out of my eight chips (2 groups
with four chips each). As far as the fit-plm-step everything seems
logical to me and I can fairly understand it. By then some questions
arise:

(1) Is there any information (besides the paper) available by now
about how FIRMA works or how to interpret the scores? How can I do a
statistical hypothesis test based on the the scores?

(2) The FirmaModel()-routine requires an object of ExonRmaPlm class
and fit() then calculates a score by exon for every array. So how do I
have to create this ExonRmaPlm-object? Do I have to use
   ... <- ExonRmaPlm(..., mergeGroups=TRUE,...)   #treat all exons
separately, only group probes
or
   ... <- ExonRmaPlm(..., mergeGroups=FALSE,...)  #merge exons into
transcripts
I suppose one could do it both ways, but which one is the more
reasonable?

(3) Since Firma calculates the score by array you should somehow merge
these values to get a score by group. Is it a good idea to simply use
the mean?

(4) What is about filtering? The Affymetrix technical note
http://www.affymetrix.com/support/technical/technotes/id_altsplicingevents_technote.pdf
suggests several steps of filtering. Is this all done by fitting the
FirmaModel? I don't see any arguments for filtering in the fit()-
method...?

(5) Is the Firma-score in any way comparable to the Splicing Index
Value?

(6) Suppose I would like to calculate a Splicing Index by myself, is
it a good idea to do something like this (as draft):
          ...  		# background correction + quantile normalization with
core-cdfs yields csN
     cdfEnsb <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(paste(chipType, "U-
Ensembl47,G-Affy", sep=","))
     setCdf(csN, cdfEnsb)
     plmExon <- ExonRmaPlm(csN,
mergeGroups=FALSE,tag=c("*","ensb"))          # contains probe set
intensities
     plmTranscript <- ExonRmaPlm(csN,
mergeGroups=TRUE,tag=c("*","ensb"))     # contains transcript cluster
intensities (right?)
# all intensities should be stored as 2^x, even though the ExonRmaPlm
doesn't inherit from AffymetrixCelSet...? Right?
     "pick an exonXY"
     splicing index of exonXY <- log2("exonXY intensity from
plmExon" / "intensity of transcript cluster containing exonXY from
plmTranscript")

I hope you can help me out with some of my questions. Thanks a lot in
advance,
Frank

Frank.

I'll provide some quick answers and Elizabeth might have more to add.

On 22/03/2008, at 11:06 AM, Frank wrote:

>
> Hi everyone,
>
> I'm pretty new in the 'exon-array-business' so hopefully my questions
> won't be too stupid...
>
> I'm using your software for some weeks now trying to get some
> information about alternative splicing out of my eight chips (2 groups
> with four chips each). As far as the fit-plm-step everything seems
> logical to me and I can fairly understand it. By then some questions
> arise:
>
> (1) Is there any information (besides the paper) available by now
> about how FIRMA works or how to interpret the scores? How can I do a
> statistical hypothesis test based on the the scores?

Generally, potential differential splice events are associated with
'extreme' FIRMA scores (i.e. large positive or large negative).  In
your case, you may be looking for differences between your 2 groups.
In the past, I have done a 'limma' analysis to look for differences
between 2 groups, operating directly on FIRMA scores.

> (2) The FirmaModel()-routine requires an object of ExonRmaPlm class
> and fit() then calculates a score by exon for every array. So how do I
> have to create this ExonRmaPlm-object? Do I have to use
>    ... <- ExonRmaPlm(..., mergeGroups=TRUE,...)   #treat all exons
> separately, only group probes
> or
>    ... <- ExonRmaPlm(..., mergeGroups=FALSE,...)  #merge exons into
> transcripts
> I suppose one could do it both ways, but which one is the more
> reasonable?

I think you have the mergeGroups logic the wrong way around.
mergeGroups=TRUE for gene-level summaries, mergeGroups=FALSE for
probeset (~exon)-level summaries.  For input to FIRMA, you'll want
mergeGroups=TRUE since FIRMA operates on the residuals from a gene-
level fit.

> (3) Since Firma calculates the score by array you should somehow merge
> these values to get a score by group. Is it a good idea to simply use
> the mean?

Depends how heterogeneous your samples are and how conservative you
want to me.  Like I said above, maybe a 'limma' analysis or something
similar would be helpful to find differences in FIRMA scores between
groups.

> (4) What is about filtering? The Affymetrix technical note
> http://www.affymetrix.com/support/technical/technotes/
> id_altsplicingevents_technote.pdf
> suggests several steps of filtering. Is this all done by fitting the
> FirmaModel? I don't see any arguments for filtering in the fit()-
> method...?

I haven't done too much filtering in my analyses so far.  I do,
however, have a look at the probe-level data and the residuals to try
and get an idea of what is happening.  FirmaModel does not do
filtering.  One thing I would be wary of is FIRMA scores that come
from 1 or 2 probes.  Most probesets have 4 probes, but extreme FIRMA
scores that come from probesets with 1 or 2 probes might be either
worth filtering out or just considering differently.

> (5) Is the Firma-score in any way comparable to the Splicing Index
> Value?

When the paper comes out, there is more description of this.  They
are not directly comparable, but generally have a positive association.

> (6) Suppose I would like to calculate a Splicing Index by myself, is
> it a good idea to do something like this (as draft):
>           ...  		# background correction + quantile normalization with
> core-cdfs yields csN
>      cdfEnsb <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(paste(chipType, "U-
> Ensembl47,G-Affy", sep=","))
>      setCdf(csN, cdfEnsb)
>      plmExon <- ExonRmaPlm(csN,
> mergeGroups=FALSE,tag=c("*","ensb"))          # contains probe set
> intensities
>      plmTranscript <- ExonRmaPlm(csN,
> mergeGroups=TRUE,tag=c("*","ensb"))     # contains transcript cluster
> intensities (right?)
> # all intensities should be stored as 2^x, even though the ExonRmaPlm
> doesn't inherit from AffymetrixCelSet...? Right?
>      "pick an exonXY"
>      splicing index of exonXY <- log2("exonXY intensity from
> plmExon" / "intensity of transcript cluster containing exonXY from
> plmTranscript")

Elizabeth may have some code for this, but this looks reasonably
close to what you want ... after the fitting and extracting
intensities, etc.  ExonRmaPlm doesn't inherit from AffymetrixCelSet
but ChipEffectSet does, which is what will contain the chip effects
that you will need.  So, yes, the intensities that you extract will
be on 2^x.  The mergeGroups is the correct way around here.

Hope that is helpful.

Cheers,
Mark

cdf <- getCdf(cesN);

Affymetrix is broken and incomplete for GWS5, cf.
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/building-ufl-file-for-genomewidesnp-5.
 In January I was told they (Affymetrix) would fix the problem rather
soon, but I haven't heard anything new for a while.  Please feel free
to write them a follow up note on the Affymetrix Forum (see link at
the above URL).

messages.subject: Problem getting started with ArrayExplorer
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I am just getting started using aroma.affymetrix, so I am trying to
run through a basic analysis of a set of HG-U133_Plus_2 arrays using
code I've collected from this group. My problem comes with trying to
display residual plots using ArrayExplorer - I get an ArrayExplorer
page (in Firefox 2.0.0.12) with a correct listing of file names, but
the display region simply shows a greatly enlarged copy of the
animated 'indicator.gif' image. Am I doing something obviously wrong?
I tried disabling all Firefox add-ons, which had no effect. Thanks for
any help...
Michael

Here's the relevant code:

library(EBImage)
library(aroma.affymetrix)
library(affyPLM)

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
timestampOn(verbose)
name <- "Project"
chipType <- "HG-U133_Plus_2"

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chipType)
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)

setCdf(cs, cdf)

# RMA background correction
bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs);
csBC <- process(bc, verbose=verbose);

# RMA quantile normalization
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm");
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose);

# RMA probe summarization
plm <- RmaPlm(csN);
fit(plm, verbose=verbose);
rs <- calculateResidualSet(plm)

ae <- ArrayExplorer(rs)
setColorMaps(ae, c("log2,log2neg,rainbow", "log2,log2pos,rainbow"))
process(ae, interleaved="auto")
display(ae)

messages.subject: Quality assessment
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

thanks for your replies in the "FIRMA Scores" Thread.

Right now I had to go one step back and try to do the quality assessment a bit more carefully. Am I right, that the only 'built-in' methods to do so are the density plots, MvA-plots and spatial plots for the raw data and RLE und NUSE plots for the plm-summarized data, right? (Furthermore you could plot residuals, errrors, weights and so on for certain units.)

But I would also like to have boxplots for raw and normalized data. I made these plots by myself (because of memery-problems this was a bit tedious and the code went ugly...) but to my suprise the boxplots of the normalized data are not like expected. Shouldn't all boxes (one boxs corresponds to one chip) be aligned in a way that all medians are equal and the IQRs are all the same? I attached both boxplots ("boxplot_raw.png" and "boxplot_RBC,QN.png"). But it seems that the normalized and bg-corrected data doesn't differ that much from the raw data! (this is also suggested by the density plots, see attachments) What do I have to think about this? (Do you need the code for inspection?)

Furthermore I would like to inspect the residuals after the plm-fit in more detail. Let me clarify my understanding of residuals first. A residual e is the difference of a measured value y and an estimated value yhat. So in general you would calculate estimates (like in getCalculateResidualsFunction.ProbeLevelModel) with e = y - yhat. If you underestimate you'll get a positive residual, if you overestimate you'll get a negative residual. But since you store the residual values in the intensities-field of an ResidualFile (which inherits AffymetrixCelFile) the residuals have to be positive. And so the function getCalculateResidualsFunction.RmaPlm() calculates e = y / yhat. So an underestimated measure corresponds with a residual > 1 and an overestimated measure corresponds with a residual < 1. Am I right so far?

 Now if I would like to identify any spatial pattern for over- or underestimation I hoped I could just do
  rs <- calculateResidualSet(...)
  rf <- getFile(rs, idx=1)
  getImage(rf, transform=list(function(x){sign(x-1)}), palette=rainbow(256), tags="sign,rainbow")
to get some sort of two-color spatial plot.
(All probes that are not included in the cdf have an estimate of zero after the fit and so would be transformed here to -1, like all overestimates. But I would accept this for a first approach.)
But all this approach yields is a spatial plot with one color. Something must have gone wrong with this transformation. I also had a look at the getImage-code where the transformation takes place but couldn't solve my problem. Did anyone create those kinds of plots or does anyone have an idea? Also I would like to create spatial plots of only the positve residuals (here residuals > 1) and plots with only negative residuals... Since I'm not sure about how to manipulate the ResidualFile directly (and maybe this isn't a very good idea) the "transform" parameter appears to be the most promising way for me.

And finally I have a question regarding (plain and simple) spatial plots of the residuals generated with
    ...
    getImage(rf, palette=rainbow(256), tags="rainbow")
ALL my plots seem to be vertically divided (see attachment "I7R_028c02,residuals,rainbow.png"). I would guess, this is not a chip-quality problem (since this applies for all chips) but some sort of systematic error in the plm-fit or so. Any experience with that?

Thanks again in advance for any kind of support,
Frank Ziegner

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Quality assessment
messages.body_plain:
Hi Frank.

Yes, we'll need the code for inspection ... and a 'sessionInfo()'
doesn't hurt.

My first impression is that you've normalized a subset of the probes
(e.g. by using the Ensembl CDF), but are plotting boxplots and
densities of the probes on the entire chip.  That's a guess.

The PLM fits are done on the log2 scale, but stored in CEL files on
the 2^ scale since they have to be positive. So, if you do a
'readUnits' on a ResidualSet, you'll need to take a log2 to get any
interpretation.  But, the calculation is definitely done as y - \hat
{y}, NOT y / \hat{y}.

I haven't done any spatial plots of residuals so I can't relate to
the details there.  You'd want to take log2 regardless to put them on
a meaningful scale.  I usually base most of my quality assessment on
RLE and NUSE plots.

About your vertically divided residual plots ... what CDF are you
using?  Since the CEL files can only store one probe effect per
probe, if a probe is part of multiple probesets, then the residual
calculations can get screwed up.  Not sure if this is related to your
problem, but its the first thing that comes to mind.

Cheers,
Mark

divided plot...? I'm still at a loss here.

projectName <- "TDP"
chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"

# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
# define CDF files (main + ensembl)
# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
cdfCore <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(paste(chipType,
"core,A20071112,EP", sep=","))

# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
# define CEL set
# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(projectName, chipType=chipType,
checkChipType=F, cdf=cdfCore)

# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
# background correction + quantile normalization
# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs,tag=c("*","core"),addJitter=T)
csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose,force=FALSE)
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN <- process(qn,force=FALSE,verbose=verbose)

# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
# fit probe level models
# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
plm_unmerged <- ExonRmaPlm(csN,
mergeGroups=FALSE,flavor=c("affyPLM"))
fit(plm_unmerged, verbose=verbose,force=FALSE)

# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
# calculate residuals
# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
rs_merged<-calculateResidualSet(plm_unmerged,verbose=verbose)

# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
# write spatial plots of residuals to file
# - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
lapply(rs_unmerged, writeImage, palette=rainbow(256), tags="rainbow")

A couple answers smattered below ...

> Hi Mark,
>
>> My first impression is that you've normalized a subset of the probes

>

> get the relevant subset of probes? I'm sure there are methods for
> this... I had a <quick> look at the identifyCells method (like it is
> used in plotDensity.AffymetrixCelFile), does this help me out?

Looks like you're sorted on this one.

> Generally I don't understand the CDF-Files very much. I checked the
> Core-CDF-File and this contains 6553600 cells. I think this is more a
> generic value because all CDF Files have the same dimensions
> (2560*2560). But how are 'core-probes' are distinguished from the
> rest? Is the rest just NA?

The CDF file is simply a collection of sets of probes, giving the physical
X,Y location of a particular probe on the chip.  aroma.affymetrix simply
figures out which indices these correspond to (in the big 2560x2560 array)
and only operates on those.  If you are interested to know more about them
(and you will if you ever need to make one), use the 'readCdf' function on
the CDF file and have a look at what info is stored there.

> So does it make sense to do a spatial plot of the residual at all,
> since you have to handle/display all the residuals of probes you
> haven't fitted (if using a core-CDF this is going to be more, if using
> extended or so more probes are fitted...) Under "Files" you can find
> some spatial plots of residuals made by Henrik (or at least uploaded
> by) named "A4,XX,residuals,+,log2,rainbow.png" which suggests, that he
> transformed the data in a way I intended to do. Maybe you can help me
> out, Henrik?
>
> On all spatial plots there is a regular pattern of rectangular white
> spaces. Are these the regions with the genomic and antigenomic
> background probes? Are these probes in any way used in aroma right
> now? I thought about a DABG-Filter... How could I access those probes?
> (This is more for the future...)

Well, you've sparked my interest here.  Like I said, I haven't used
spatial plots for exon array data, but thats not to say they are
uninformative.  I'll try and see if I can recreate what you see.

>> About your vertically divided residual plots ... what CDF are you
>> using?  Since the CEL files can only store one probe effect per
>> probe, if a probe is part of multiple probesets, then the residual
>> calculations can get screwed up.  Not sure if this is related to your
>> problem, but its the first thing that comes to mind.
>
> Hm, I'm not sure if I'm understanding you... By probe effect you mean
> probe affinity, right? This is stored once for all chips in the file
> "probeAffinities.CEL". But why can the residual calculation get
> screwed up? For a given probeset $i$ you have one to four measured
> signals/probes $y_ij$ with $1 \leq j \leq 4$. If you call
> ExonRmaPlm(...,mergeGroups=FALSE,...) you'll have only one estimate
> \hat{y_i} per probeset, right? (See code below for cdf-File
> specification)  That is the idea of summarizing the data, or not? So
> how are the residuals PER PROBE calculated? $r_ij = y_ij - \hat{y_i}$
> I guess? And all residuals are stored in a seperate CEL file.
> So I would say, there is no problem in calculating (or storing) the
> residuals for a probe in a multiple probeset. And even if that would
> be a problem, I can't see why this would result in such a vertically
> divided plot...? I'm still at a loss here.

First of all, I don't think this is related to your problem, because you
are using the 'core' CDF created by Elizabeth and that has been checked to
not have probes in multiple probesets.

It's off topic now, but just so you understand what I mean about the probe
effects thing, I'll try to be more clear.  Say y_{ij} is the data for
SAMPLE i (not probeset as you mention above) and probe j (j=1,...,4 for
example).  Residuals are calculated as:

r_{ij} = y_{ij} - \hat{a}_i - \hat{p}_j

where a_i are the chip effects and p_j are the probe effects.
aroma.affymetrix comes along, fits these models separately for each probe
set and stores the a_i (in a _chipEffects.CEL file?) and p_j (in
probeAffinities.CEL).  But, you can only store one probe effect for any
probe, so if a probe is part of multiple probesets, only one will get
stored.  Since the residuals rely on these (in a later calculation where
everything is read back from the various CEL files), there can be
problems.  I know of a way to avoid this whole problem as it pertains to
residuals (and that is to store the residuals as they are calculated from
the 'preprocessCore' routines instead of calculating them afterwards), but
that is not implemented yet.

Long winded answer.

Cheers,
Mark

Just write an email to aroma-af...@googlegroups.com from your email
account (i.e. not w/n google groups)

I have not found a satisfactory solution yet. But as Mark says, I usually just use the NUSE and RLE boxplots because I have too many arrays to inspect them, though I have wanted to occassionally look at a particular one. You can always at least look at the intensity. However, since so many of those probes will be at background, the plot will still probably not be so informative.

> background probes? Are these probes in any way used in aroma right
> now? I thought about a DABG-Filter... How could I access those probes?

So those spots are griding spots to help the scanner align itself -- I don't know the details of it. That's why they light up in that regular way. But there are the background probes you refer to. They are not currently used for anything, but I have looked at them. The way I do this is to grep the Affy annotation to get the probset names and then use the default (Affy-provided) cdf to access them and get their cell indices for things like density plots. They are not included in the Core cdf. They look pretty much like the density plot of all the probes, which is maybe not so surprising given the large number of speculative probes on the array which are probably also at background.

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with Fragment Length Normalization
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with Fragment Length Normalization
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

sorry for the delay  - I just had and will have some more busy weeks
ahead of me.

You seem to have the correct CDF and UFL files for GWS5.

The main problem, as I mentioned earlier, is that the fragment
information for GWS5 is only partly correct and that causes the
problem.  I believe that when we get the correct information from
Affymetrix your problem will go away.  Without the correct annotation
data, it is be better for you to skip the fragment-length
normalization step.

However, if you want troubleshoot further, here is what goes on.  When
you apply the allelic-crosstalk calibration you will introduce a
fraction of non-positive probe signals (this is because some
homozygote SNPs have true allele signal zero for one of the alleles,
and then we add noise, but also because some signals are very close to
the signal-to-noise levels).  Some of the non-positive signals will
carry through to the summarized signals, the averaging over 3-4 SNP
probes lower the fraction, but some still gets through.  For CN probes
you will also get some non-positive signals.   The fragment-length
normalization is modeling the data on the log2 scale, meaning
non-positive signals will be NAs.  This is normally not a problem
because there should be enough of finite log2 signals to fit the
effects.  However, for multi-enzyme chip types such as GWS5 and GWS6,
we stratify on loci exclusively on one enzyme, and because a large
fraction of loci are on both enzymes we have a smaller pool to fit the
model.  If you then have NAs in your data, the number of data points
gets even smaller.   In your case the intersect of valid data points
and loci exclusively on Enzyme #2 is zero.  I have committed some
patches allowing you to get more details about the number of
non-negative signals, valid loci etc.  Do:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

Then, when you have defined your FragmentLengthNormalization object:

fcns <- getTargetFunctions(fln, force=TRUE, verbose=-20)

Look at the verbose output, which will give some details.  It might
reveal that you've got a lot of non-positive chip-effect estimates
(hope not).

Moreover, there is an option to add a small offset to data before
taking the log, e.g.

fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(cs, shift=+200)
fcns <- getTargetFunctions(fln, force=TRUE, verbose=-20)

That might give you less NAs on the log2 scale.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.body_plain:

sorry for the delay.

On Tue, Mar 25, 2008 at 10:21 AM, michael <Michael...@fccc.edu> wrote:
>
>  Hello,
>  I am just getting started using aroma.affymetrix, so I am trying to
>  run through a basic analysis of a set of HG-U133_Plus_2 arrays using
>  code I've collected from this group. My problem comes with trying to
>  display residual plots using ArrayExplorer - I get an ArrayExplorer
>  page (in Firefox 2.0.0.12) with a correct listing of file names, but
>  the display region simply shows a greatly enlarged copy of the
>  animated 'indicator.gif' image. Am I doing something obviously wrong?
>  I tried disabling all Firefox add-ons, which had no effect. Thanks for
>  any help...
>  Michael

You have found a bug that was introduced in aroma.affymetrix v0.9.0
causing the ArrayExplorer (actually a helper class) to output the
images in a directory that has replicated tags.  For instance, in your
case the PNG files should have been saved to:

  reports/Project/RBC,QN,RMA/HG-U133_Plus_2/spatial/

but they ended up in:

  reports/Project/RBC,QN,RMA,RBC,QN,RMA/HG-U133_Plus_2/spatial/

If you move those PNG files in the 2nd path to the first path, the
ArrayExplorer should display the plots as expected.

I have committed a patch that fixes the above.  To install the patch, do:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

More comments about your script below.

>
>  Here's the relevant code:
>
>  library(EBImage)
>  library(aroma.affymetrix)
>  library(affyPLM)
>
>  verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
>  timestampOn(verbose)
>  name <- "Project"

>  cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chipType)
>  cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType)
>
>  setCdf(cs, cdf)

FYI, you do not have to setup the 'cdf' and call setCdf() here; the
default CDF is set by default and it is only when you use a custom CDF
when you have to do that.

Cheers

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

sorry for the delay.

On Wed, Mar 26, 2008 at 9:28 PM, Roger <rpi...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>  Dear Dr. H Bengtsson,
>
>  I recently discovered the aroma.affymetrix package, I really like the
>  method and I'm
>  very interested in using it to do the preprocessing before applying my
>  copy
>  number segmentation algorithm:
>  http://bioinformatics.oxfordjournals.org/cgi/content/short/24/3/309
>
>  I also plan to evaluate it on the entire 270 Hapmap Affy6.0 reference
>  samples.
>  I already did a test run with the example you provide using CBS on the
>  google group.
>
>  I already have some experience in using CBS so I would really
>  appreciate
>  if you could tell me which would be the functions that I should modify
>  in
>  aroma.affymetrix so I can replace the CBS by my algorithm.
>  I would really appreciate your help.

Great that you consider adding a class for your GADA method.  You need
to create a subclass GadaModel of the abstract class
CopyNumberSegmentationModel.  This is as easy as:

setConstructorS3("GadaModel", function(...) {
  extend(CopyNumberSegmentationModel(...), "GadaModel")
})

Then you need to provide a method getAsteriskTags() that returns the
tag(s) replacing any tag "*":

setMethodS3("getAsteriskTags", "GadaModel", function(this, collapse=NULL, ...) {
  tags <- "GADA";
  if (isPaired(this))
    tags <- c(tags, "paired");
  tags <- paste(tags, collapse=collapse);
  tags;
}, protected=TRUE)

Already now you can try the following, assuming you have a
CnChipEffectSet object named 'ces' :

> gada <- GadaModel(ces);
> print(gada);
> print(getPath(gada));

Note how the "root" path of your GadaModel starts with 'gadaData/'.
That is the output path where (you will) store you model
estimates/results.  Download the source of aroma.affymetrix and you
will see how this is done for CbsModel in source file R/CbsModel.R.

You can now even try the following:

> fit(gada, arrays=1:2, chromosomes=22, verbose=-20);

You'll see it that the framework will load the chip effects for the
chromosomes of interest, calculate the raw CN (log2 ratios) and try to
call fitOne() on your GadaModel object.  As you see you will get an
error because you still haven't define fitOne() for the GadaModel
class.  This is the method that will take the data and do the fitting
etc and return the results.

fitOne() should take an argument 'data' which is a Jx6 matrix where
the number of rows J is the number of loci, and the six columns are x,
M, sdTheta, sdM, chipType, and unit.  To understand what this object
is, try:

> files <- getMatrixChipEffectFiles(gada, array=1);
> ceList <- files[,"test"];
> refList <- files[,"reference"];
> data <- getRawCnData(gada, ceList=ceList, refList=refList, chromosome=22, verbose=-10);
> str(data)
 num [1:74, 1:6] 15685581 16604328 16958128 17506879 18008688 ...
 - attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
  ..$ : NULL
  ..$ : chr [1:6] "x" "M" "sdTheta" "sdM" ...
> plot(data[,c("x","M")], ylim=c(-3,3))

So, 'x' is the genomic position, 'M' is the log2 ratio.  These are
probably the only ones you will need.  [The 'sdM' ('sdTheta') is the
estimated standard of each M (theta), and 'chiptype' and 'unit' is the
chip type and the CDF unit index for the particular locus.  The 'chip
type' is useful if data from two or more chip type are to be
segmented.]

Assume you have an R function fitGada(x,M) that takes positions 'x'
and log-ratios 'M' and identifies CN regions returned in some
structure.  For simplicity, assume the return structure is of class
"GadaFit".  Then your fitOne() should look something like (excluding
any 'verbose' statements):

setMethodS3("fitOne", "GadaModel", function(this, data, ..., verbose=FALSE) {
  fit <- fitGada(x=data[,"x"], M=data[,"M"]);
  # In case your fitGada() does not return an object with class, then do
  # class(fit) <- "GadaFit"
  # In case your fitGada() does not return the raw CNs, add them here
  # fit$data <- data;
  fit;
}, private=TRUE) # fitOne()

You probably want to add verbose output etc.  See how this is done for
the CbsModel (see R/CbsModel.fitOne.R).  You can also look how it is
done for the GladModel.

You next have to write a extractRawCopyNumbers() for "GadaFit" that
returns a RawCopyNumber object, e.g.

setMethodS3("extractRawCopyNumbers", "GadaFit", functionfunction (fit, ...) {
    data <- fitt$data;
    RawCopyNumbers(cn=data[,"M"], x=data[,"x"])
})

and extractCopyNumberRegions() for "GadaFit" that returns a
CopyNumberRegions object, e.g.

setMethodS3("extractCopyNumberRegions", "GadaFit", function (fit, ...) {
    CopyNumberRegions(chromosome=fit[,"chr"], start=fit[,"start"],
stop=fit[,"stop"],
              mean=fit[,"meanLevel"], count=fit[,"nbrOfLoci"]);
})

That should be it (but I might have forgot something).  Hope this get
you started.  So look at CbsModel/GladModel and what methods are
called in fit() of the CopyNumberSegmentationModel class.  Turn on
maximum verbose output, e.g. verbose=-50 when you call fit() to see
what data is passed and where you get errors etc.

I'll be happy to add the your segmentation class aroma.affymetrix when
you get it up and running.

Cheers

Henrik

>
>  Best regards,
>  >
>

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Quality assessment
messages.body_plain:
Elizabeth,

Where we may want probes to be in multiple probesets is in a CDF that is transcript-based instead of gene-based.  For comparing specific transcripts instead of lumping them all into a gene for differential analysis.  I'm probably going to make one of these in the next round of Ensembl CDFs (I've just been reminded that Ensembl 49 is out).  Though, in this case, you are probably not interested in residuals, at least in the FIRMA sense, but it does create problems if you are interested in looking at the residuals for quality assessment purposes.

Mark

On 29/03/2008, at 3:23 PM, Elizabeth Purdom wrote:

> Just a small comment that I've probably made before. But I'm really not sure what the value of providing an option that deals with this 'problem' (that we can't store multiple residuals per probe) -- though a warning might be nice. I can't think of situations where this is really interesting, though I'm sure someone can tell me. If the probe is legitimately mapping to more than one gene, say because of overlapping genes, then I don't think the overlap is going to be interpretable in terms of alternative splicing, unless you are sure that one gene is absolutely not expressed. I don't like the Affy option of rolling the genes together; I prefer throwing out such regions and keeping the genes distinct, particularly if you are just looking at core or ensembl probesets anyway.
>
> Just a thought,
> Elizabeth
>
> >
> > First of all, I don't think this is related to your problem, because you
> > are using the 'core' CDF created by Elizabeth and that has been checked to
> > not have probes in multiple probesets.
> >
> > It's off topic now, but just so you understand what I mean about the probe
> > effects thing, I'll try to be more clear.  Say y_{ij} is the data for
> > SAMPLE i (not probeset as you mention above) and probe j (j=1,...,4 for
> > example).  Residuals are calculated as:
> >
> > r_{ij} = y_{ij} - \hat{a}_i - \hat{p}_j
> >
> > where a_i are the chip effects and p_j are the probe effects.
> > aroma.affymetrix comes along, fits these models separately for each probe
> > set and stores the a_i (in a _chipEffects.CEL file?) and p_j (in
> > probeAffinities.CEL).  But, you can only store one probe effect for any
> > probe, so if a probe is part of multiple probesets, only one will get
> > stored.  Since the residuals rely on these (in a later calculation where
> > everything is read back from the various CEL files), there can be
> > problems.  I know of a way to avoid this whole problem as it pertains to
> > residuals (and that is to store the residuals as they are calculated from
> > the 'preprocessCore' routines instead of calculating them afterwards), but
> > that is not implemented yet.
> >
> > Long winded answer.
> >
> > Cheers,
> > Mark
> >
> >
> > > (P.S.: How can I attach a file when answering via this front-end and
> > > not by mail? There is no "attachment"-button here...)
> >
> > Just write an email to aroma-af...@googlegroups.com from your email
> > account (i.e. not w/n google groups)
> >
> >
> >
> >
>
>
>

>  what versions you are using?
>
>  2. What CDF file are you using and where did you get it from?

Yes, it is not a memory problem or that you data set is too big.
Instead, my best guess is that you have one or more corrupted CEL
files.  The crash/core dump is happening when calling affxparser
(based on Fusion SDK), which is the package used to read CEL files.
We are aware that affxparser has problems and can crash R if corrupt
files are used.  We hope to add exception handling to affxparser at
some stage prevent it from crashing and instead returning a nice error
message.

To figure out what CEL file(s) might cause the problem, do this:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HuEx-1_0-st-v2", tags="core");
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("BcExonArray", cdf=cdf);
for (kk in seq(cs)) {
  cf <- getFile(cs, kk);
  pathname <- getPathname(cf);
  print(list(kk=kk, pathname=pathname, fi=file.info <http://file.info>(pathname)));
  print(cf);
}

Most likely this will crash when print(cf) is done on a corrupt CEL
file.  This way you will be able to identify the bad CEL files and
most likely there is an obvious answer why they are corrupt.

/Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

namespaces are supposed to handle this and I guess it might not have
been a problem if aroma.affymetrix had a namespace.  Unfortunately it
is not straightforward to add a namespace to aroma.affymetrix.  Last
time I tried it caused some side effects, but you are welcome to try
and see if it works.

Alternatively, if you load the "other" package before
aroma.affymetrix, then aroma.affymetrix will be ahead of the other
package on the search list and getNames() should be found as expected.
 aroma.affymetrix defined getNames() as a generic function so the
other package should still work.  In R.utils there is even the
moveInSearchPath() method that allows you to reorder the search() path
after loading the package.  That might be handy as well.

Let us know if this solves your problem.

Henrik

If anything is unclear in those docs, please let me/us know.

Also, there is an online Vignette 'Total copy number analysis (10K,
100K, 500K)', so there is no need for you to follow the 'Total Copy
Number Analysis (5.0 & 6.0)' vignette.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
A quick follow up on this:  I have located the bug in
getTableOfArrays() causing the segmentation model to give an error on
invalid indices.  Note, you still have to solve the cause of the
problem of naming you files according to the <name>,<tags> format in
order for aroma.affymetrix to be able to pair up hybridizations from
different chip types.  In other words, with the bug fix but still with
the incorrect filenames, you would no longer get an error, but instead
aroma.affymetrix would infer that you have used 30+30 arrays where
half is for one chip type and the other half on the other.  This would
result in 60 segmented "samples".  So, make sure to get your filenames
right.

/Henrik

I have committed a patch that fixes the above.  To install the patch, do:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

messages.body_snippet:
A quick follow up on this:  I have located the bug in
getTableOfArrays() causing the segmentation model to give an error on
invalid indices.  Note, you still have to solve the cause of the
problem of

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: question about an error displayed after fit(glad)
messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: question about an error displayed after fit(glad)
messages.body_plain:
Forgot to say, until next release, the bug fix can be installed as a patch:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

/Henrik

On Mon, Mar 31, 2008 at 1:32 PM, Henrik Bengtsson <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
> A quick follow up on this:  I have located the bug in
>  getTableOfArrays() causing the segmentation model to give an error on
>  invalid indices.  Note, you still have to solve the cause of the
>  problem of naming you files according to the <name>,<tags> format in
>  order for aroma.affymetrix to be able to pair up hybridizations from
>  different chip types.  In other words, with the bug fix but still with
>  the incorrect filenames, you would no longer get an error, but instead
>  aroma.affymetrix would infer that you have used 30+30 arrays where
>  half is for one chip type and the other half on the other.  This would
>  result in 60 segmented "samples".  So, make sure to get your filenames
>  right.
>
>  /Henrik
>
>  I have committed a patch that fixes the above.  To install the patch, do:
>
>  library(aroma.affymetrix);
>  downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");
>
>
>
>

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark and Henrik,

Thanks for your reply. I checked with the code Henrik
suggested and found about 20 arrays are corrupted, I
guess it is due to my way of "copy and paste" files,
or due to the way I transferred files between
different working stations using "sftp".

Anyway, the problem is solved, I transferred my files
again from the original resources and now it seems
work well. Many thanks for your kind help!

Shuying

--- Henrik Bengtsson <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:

>
> Hi.
>
> On Sun, Mar 30, 2008 at 10:03 PM, Mark Robinson
> <mrob...@wehi.edu.au> wrote:
> >
> >  Shuying.
> >
> >  The number of arrays is definitely NOT too large.
>  I have done >125
> >  exon chips on a small computer.  You should be
> able to run
> >  aroma.affymetrix with very little memory (<
> 500Mb).
> >
> >  A couple quick queries:
> >
> >  1. Can you give the results of 'sessionInfo()' so
> we know exactly
> >  what versions you are using?
> >
> >  2. What CDF file are you using and where did you
> get it from?
>
> Yes, it is not a memory problem or that you data set
> is too big.
> Instead, my best guess is that you have one or more
> corrupted CEL
> files.  The crash/core dump is happening when
> calling affxparser
> (based on Fusion SDK), which is the package used to
> read CEL files.
> We are aware that affxparser has problems and can
> crash R if corrupt
> files are used.  We hope to add exception handling
> to affxparser at
> some stage prevent it from crashing and instead
> returning a nice error
> message.
>
> To figure out what CEL file(s) might cause the
> problem, do this:
>
> library(aroma.affymetrix);
> cdf <-
> AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HuEx-1_0-st-v2",
> tags="core");
> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("BcExonArray",
> cdf=cdf);
> for (kk in seq(cs)) {
>   cf <- getFile(cs, kk);
>   pathname <- getPathname(cf);
>   print(list(kk=kk, pathname=pathname,
> fi=file.info <http://file.info>(pathname)));
>   print(cf);
> }
>
> Most likely this will crash when print(cf) is done
> on a corrupt CEL
> file.  This way you will be able to identify the bad
> CEL files and
> most likely there is an obvious answer why they are
> corrupt.
>
> /Henrik
>
>
> >
> >
> >  Mark
> >
> >
> >
> >
> >
> >
> >  On 31/03/2008, at 3:51 PM, Shuying wrote:
> >
> >  >
> >  > Hello,
> >  >
> >  > I am a beginner of exon array analysis and
> >  > aroma.affymetrix, the R program I ran crashed
> and left
> >  > the following message:
> >  > ------------------------------
> >  > terminate called after throwing an instance of
> >  >
>
'affymetrix_calvin_exceptions::UnableToOpenFileException'
> >  > Abort
> >  > -----------------------------
> >  >
> >  > Here is the story: my laptop computer is MAC. I
> have
> >  > 41 exon arrays (HuEx-1_0-st-v2), the total file
> size
> >  > is about 2GB.
> >  > I first install the latest version of R (Feb
> 2008
> >  > version) and aroma.affymetrix, and when I run
> the the
> >  > following basic code:
> >  >
> >  > library(aroma.affymetrix)
> >  > chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
> >  > cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType,
> >  > tags="core")
> >  > print(cdf)
> >  > BC.exon <-
> AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("BcExonArray",
> >  > cdf=cdf)
> >  > print(BC.exon)
> >  >
> >  > --- When I run the above "print(BC.exon)", I
> got:
> >  > # > print(BC.exon)
> >  > # terminate called after throwing an instance
> of
> >  > 'affymetrix_calvin_exceptions::UnableToO
> >  > # penFileException'
> >  > # Abort trap
> >  >
> >  > But when I try only 4 arrays, it works well, so
> I
> >  > thought two reasons might explain this:
> >  > 1) the number of arrays are too large
> >  > 2) my laptop computer is not powerful
> >  >
> >  > Later I switch to other powerful working
> stations at
> >  > berkeley stats and LBL, when I tried to use

> >  > R crashed again and I got the same message
> again.

'affymetrix_calvin_exceptions::UnableToOpenFileException'
